en.title: Silicon Valley’s AI wunderkind launches Underdog, the most private Instinct/Muse competitor yet
en.summary: Sigil Wen, backed by a Silicon Valley who's who, has built an on-device AI assistant that promises to be free, fully private, and capable for everyday tasks.
en.body:
When self-taught coder Sigil Wen was 17, he moved to Silicon Valley and lived in an AI hacker house with famed AI researcher Andrej Karpathy.

While there, he hacked and coded alongside other people who would become the biggest names in AI, like Perplexity founder Aravind Srinivas and OpenAI researcher Noam Brown. He tested early versions of AI tools that would later become well known, including a chatbot shared by Anthropic co-founder Ben Mann that would become Claude, an image generator from David Holz that would become Midjourney, and what would become OpenAI’s GPT-3 and the image generator Stable Diffusion. Prominent investor and entrepreneur Naval Ravikant hired him for Airchat, Ravikant’s now-defunct rival to the Clubhouse social network.

For fun, he figured out how to get GPT-2 running on his Apple Watch. “It was a magical time,” Wen told TechCrunch.

Now a Thiel Fellow — the program from investor Peter Thiel that invites young founders to pursue projects instead of college — Wen on Monday launched an invite-only beta of Underdog, one of the most private AI assistants Silicon Valley has yet to offer. The model runs wholly on-device, meaning the user’s data remains on devices they already own, currently Macs and Windows PCs, with Linux, iPhone, and Android versions coming soon.

Wen built Husky, an inference engine, or software that runs AI models, and Husky is designed to run fast. Unlike other on-device engines, Wen says, it moves less data between the computer’s main chip and its graphics chip.

Underdog has other security features baked in, too, like encrypting the keys to the email and other accounts that users authorize Underdog to access.

Underdog is, however, using much smaller models than today’s state-of-the-art ones hosted in data centers. It currently uses a 27-billion parameter reasoning model fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B.

Wen argues that this model compares favorably with Claude Opus 4.6 in some benchmarks , or what was considered top performance six months ago. He says that means it can handle the everyday tasks that people want an AI assistant to do, like shopping research or answering math homework questions.

“You don’t need to sacrifice your privacy for the capability because they’re just as capable,” Wen says. He adds that small on-device models will continue to grow more capable over time.

Perhaps the most interesting thing about Underdog is its early business model. The app will be free at first and never ad-supported. Since the AI runs on users’ machines, Underdog doesn’t have the giant overhead of paying a provider for inference. “I don’t have to charge you a subscription to run this because my costs are so super low,” he said.

Instead, with Stripe co-founder Patrick Collison as one of his angel investors, he’s borrowing a play from the fintech era. Underdog will take a tiny percentage of payment transactions that the AI assistant makes using Stripe’s secure payment rails, something like an interchange fee. In this way, the AI assistant never has to mine your data. It is as aligned with you as your bank or credit card providers.

This runs contrary to the business motivations of many of the other players in AI assistants, whose privacy policies allow them to collect data on users that they may sell to advertisers or other third parties, or use to train other models.

That kind of data collection could be a particularly treacherous trade-off for users of an AI assistant, which may need access to the most intimate details about you in order to be useful, from medical conditions to financial data to data on your kids.

As Wen wrote in what he calls his AI manifesto , “Why should using AI require surrendering your private information?”

He tells TechCrunch: “I honestly want to build Underdog for myself. I’m building a product that I would be proud for my future children to use.”

The startup behind Underdog is named Conway Research, and Collison isn’t its only big-name investor. Conway is backed by Andreessen Horowitz via partner Chris Dixon, as well as Khosla Ventures, Hummingbird, SV Angel, the Anthology Fund (the partnership fund between Menlo Ventures and Anthropic), and a prominent list of angel investors that includes Vercel founder Guillermo Rauch, Noam Brown, and Deedy Das, among others.

en.title: How AI decision models could change content moderation
en.summary: On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B, released with open weights.
en.body:
As decision models spread across the industry, a company called Musubi has a new idea for how to put them to work: moderating content. On Tuesday, Musubi announced a lightweight decision model made for real-time moderation called PolicyLM-1.7B , released with open weights.

The idea is to take a content policy written in plain English and apply it to messages in under 50 milliseconds. Musubi’s model is designed to be similar in cost and speed to the AI classifier systems that power moderation on most social platforms — but because it has the flexibility of a modern LLM, it can apply complex policies without special training. Even more important, the model won’t need new training when the policy changes, allowing for human policy-setters to iterate as much as they need.

As Musubi co-founder and chief AI officer Filip Jankovic sees it, it gives platform managers a way to label content proactively.

“Product teams just want a better understanding of what’s happening on their platform, especially as the amount of content is exponentially increasing,” Jankovic says. “Being able to label all of that in a very scalable, customizable way is extremely useful.”

Decision models have become a hot topic in the AI world since the release of TypeSafe AI’s Jev in September , which was shortly followed by competing decision models from OpenAI and Amazon . Instead of outputting text, a decision model outputs outcome probabilities, though in this case the model outputs a binary judgement: Either the content is in the category or it isn’t. By limiting the model’s output to a set of predetermined choices, decision models are able to run faster and cheaper than large language models, while still maintaining the flexibility of the transformer architecture.

One early use case is reining in misbehavior by AI agents — so it’s only natural to apply the same technology to human misbehavior.

Notably, Jankovic says his interest in decision models predates Jev, tracing it back to a 2024 project called GLiNER (Generalist Model for Named Entity Recognition) that deployed many of the same techniques.

Still, Musubi isn’t wary of the comparison. If anything, the company is eager to use the new interest in decision models to shine a light on content moderation. “If Jev caught your eye, PolicyLM-1.7B is the same kind of model, trained specifically for content moderation, that you can run yourself,” the product announcement reads.

en.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
en.summary: Personal AI agents promise to shop, book flights, and make reservations for you. But deliberate blocks and anti-bot defenses are getting in the way, leaving consumers caught in the middle. A new standard aims to help.
en.body:
Personal AI agents, like Meta’s Muse, Instinct, ChatGPT’s Dots, and others, are kicking off a new wave of consumer AI that involves more than just responding to queries. These AI agents can actually get things done on users’ behalf, like booking flights, making dinner reservations, ordering groceries, and more, all without having to be technical enough to set up OpenClaw or some other agent on your own computer.

But consumers adopting these agents are often running into issues when the website on the other end of their request blocks the AI from completing the job.

Most recently, Amazon began blocking Meta’s Muse AI agent from its retail site, meaning that the agent could no longer browse or make purchases from its product catalog.

However, the problem is not limited to Amazon or Muse. User complaints across social media indicate their agents are often running into similar blocks. Some of these are intentional, like Amazon’s, while others are the result of websites’ traditional anti-bot measures designed to protect against spam and malicious activity.

What’s not clear to the end user is whether or not the block is accidental on the website owner’s part, which leaves them frustrated with both the service provider or retailer and the agent trying to facilitate the transaction.

For instance, TechCrunch has seen a han d ful of complaints on social media claiming that Muse couldn’t complete a purchase on Walmart’s retail website. ( NBC also reported that this was a problem Walmart had faced in its tests of the AI agent.)

But a spokesperson for Walmart told us these weren’t intentional. In fact, Walmart is partnered with Muse, as was announced at Meta’s Connect developer conference in September. The company said it wants to be where its customers are, and that now includes being available through AI agent experiences.

The issue that Walmart customers often appear to be running into (see below) is that the website presents a button that has to be clicked to verify the visitor is human. If that experience is interrupted, the check could fail, and the agent gets booted out.

It’s an indication that the current technology we use to verify humans and keep websites safe from spam and bots may not be the best fit for the agent-first era of the web we’re now moving into.

To address this problem, industry partners including Meta, Walmart, Stripe, Sierra, Genesys, Rocket, NiCE, and Decagon have begun working on an open standard that would dictate how AI agents can communicate with businesses, helping to separate the good bots acting on behalf of the user and the bad. This protocol will be specifically focused on agent-to-agent communication for the purposes of online commerce, Meta said in a blog post.

In the meantime, consumer confusion abounds.

Although Walmart is at least trying to be accessible via AI agents, other companies aren’t so keen on the idea or haven’t fully embraced the technology.

For example, flight booking is currently one of the main use cases being positioned for agents, but many people have reported issues with airlines rejecting their agents’ requests.

Delta, for instance, told us that the company is taking steps to protect customers from unauthorized automated activity, and that if it were to open up to AI agents, it would have to be done with “security and the customer experience in mind.”

“While Delta does not currently have a partnership or integration that enables a third-party AI agent to shop for or book Delta flights on a customer’s behalf on our digital platforms, we’re continuing to evaluate how new technology, including external AI agents, could enhance the way customers engage with Delta,” said Delta’s general manager of Global Communications, Heena Chavda, in response to our questions about whether or not it was blocking agents, as some users complained.

United was not quite as direct as Delta, but a spokesperson pointed us to the part of its Terms of Use policy, which says that the user agrees “not to use any robot, spider, other automatic device, or manual process to monitor or copy this website or the content contained therein or for any other unauthorized purpose without United’s prior written permission.” (United didn’t respond to a follow-up question about whether it was blocking specific personal AI agents, like Muse.)

Early adopters’ complaints across social media have referenced a number of brands that are reportedly blocking AI agents, including Yelp , eBay , Zillow , Pizza Hut , Adidas , and various airlines . Some believe that the blocking activity seems to have recently increased .

A couple of people even said eBay suspended their accounts because of their use of agentic AI. Another complained that Google kicked out Instinct while it was cleaning up their Gmail inbox for them.

Despite the push to have agents book tables at restaurants and other tedious tasks, Yelp told us that it doesn’t permit non-human traffic on its platform unless the agent has paid to access Yelp’s content and data through its data licensing program . That means agents trying to use its site to get a quote, add a user to a waitlist, or book them a table will likely fail if they don’t have a formal partnership with Yelp.

eBay told TechCrunch that its approach is not to prohibit all third-party shopping agents from completing purchases. Instead, its policies restrict unauthorized agents and actions, like automated scraping and model training.

Adidas, Zillow, and Pizza Hut either didn’t respond or declined to provide a comment by the time of publication.

One major company involved in this space is Cloudflare, which offers sites protection from AI agents that could be training on its data and managing other automated activity. Some suspect that Cloudflare and other content delivery networks (CDNs) like it are currently disrupting Muse traffic. This is attributed to a change to crawler defaults on September 15, which allows site owners to block AI training while allowing other types of bots. Existing sites that were previously set to block AI bots for security reasons were then shifted to block AI agents on any pages that had ads.

However, when we asked if Cloudflare had any insight into what was happening with the blocking of these personal AI agents, like Muse and others, the company said it didn’t have any specific data to share at this time. It pointed us instead to its free public data hub, Cloudflare Radar . The site shows the increase in bot activity (which Cloudflare has also commented on previously), but it doesn’t help differentiate between the good bots and the bad ones.

Cloudflare also has a vested interest in mitigating AI traffic to websites, as it now runs a marketplace where AI bots have to pay for the data they access. It recently began testing a new web browser built specifically for AI agents.

Given the rapidly evolving space, Meta’s decision to form specific brand partnerships for Muse access seems to be the right way to go, as is its decision to focus on new standards. In doing so, it assures its customers that its agent, at least, is welcome at these partners’ sites — so any issues with access would be reportable bugs.

Meta also maintains a list of “connectors” (a.k.a. partners) inside the Muse app, which continues to grow. Many of Meta’s newly announced partners haven’t yet shown up in this list. But given Muse’s rapid expansion , which now includes partnered tools for small businesses , a bigger reorganization of Muse’s connector list is likely soon to be underway.

“Turning away a personal agent means turning away the customer behind it. We’d rather work with businesses to address the underlying concerns than see them lose that customer,” Meta said in its announcement about the newly announced plans to develop a standard. “There is a path that is good for users and good for businesses. It starts with clear norms, gives businesses more predictable control, and evolves toward a more efficient way for agents to work together.”

en.title: iOS 27.2 beta 3: Here’s everything new
en.summary: Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers yesterday, and it includes a handful of changes and hints at future features. Here’s everything new in the latest beta. more…
en.body:
Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 3 to developers yesterday, and it includes a handful of changes and hints at future features. Here’s everything new in the latest beta.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony : Sony is running a massive sale on its best BRAVIA TVs, ranging from its entry-level to flagship options — shop now to save !

Apple released iOS 27.2 beta 3 on Monday for developers, with build number 24B5099f. It comes two weeks after the release of the second beta. A new public beta was released on Tuesday, ahead of a final release to everyone before the end of the month.

New Apple Music logo

Apple teased a new Apple Music logo when it announced Apple Music Hall last month, and iOS 27.2 beta 3 suggests it’s about to roll out everywhere. The new logo uses a bolder typeface than the old logo, plus a lowercase “m” in “music.”

Apple has also started rolling it out to the Apple Music sign-up flow in iOS 27.2 beta 3.

New Messages settings in the works

Code references in iOS 27.2 beta 3 suggest Apple is working on a new setting that gives users more control over the suggested actions that appear in the Messages app, such as the “Add to Calendar” button.

The code hints that you’ll be able to disable suggested actions for individual apps, including Calendar, Reminders, Notes, and Maps. The change isn’t actually enabled yet, and it’s possible Apple scraps it before releasing it.

Apple Books design tweaks

As spotted by Beta Profiles on X , iOS 27.2 beta 3 brings new Liquid Glass design changes to the Apple Books app. There’s also a new progress bar for tracking your progress when reading a book.

Ryan has some more details on it here.

macOS 27.2 beta 3: Touchscreen Mac hints

Apple is expected to unveil the touchscreen MacBook Pro as soon as this month. macOS 27.2 beta 3 includes even more hints at Apple’s work optimizing macOS to support touch interactions. The update includes new “gesture recognition tools” for several stock Apple apps.

There’s also a new long-press animation for the Dock that seems perfect for touch interaction:

More tidbits

en.title: Don't throw away your old digital camera — do this instead
en.summary: Your old camera might give video calls an upgrade, as long as USB support or clean HDMI keeps the setup sensible.
en.body:
Your old camera might give video calls an upgrade.

Old digital cameras are making a weird comeback, so it may feel a bit more difficult to justify throwing one in the electronics recycling bin than it would have a few years ago. According to the Camera & Imaging Products Association, shipments of built-in-lens digital cameras grew 29.6 percent in 2025 to approximately 2.44 million units, and are projected to increase an additional 13.6 percent in 2026. (CIPA didn't attribute that growth specifically to the current trend of retro digicams.)

If you already have one lying around, however, there's another reason to keep it. There are a lot of older DSLRs, mirrorless cameras and even some compact cameras that can be used as webcams. That can translate to improved low-light performance, greater control over framing or the natural background blur that laptop webcams devote a lot of software to trying to replicate. The trick is finding out whether yours can do it without turning a free upgrade into an expensive side project.

Start with the specific model number and the manufacturer's webcam compatibility list. Canon's EOS 6D and EOS Rebel T6 are still supported, as are Nikon's D5300 and D750 with its Webcam Utility and Sony's A5100, A7 II and RX100 IV with Imaging Edge Webcam.

If your camera is listed, then setup can be rather simple. Install the manufacturer's webcam software if required, connect the camera using a USB data cable , put it into the appropriate video or remote mode and select it as the camera in Zoom, Google Meet or Microsoft Teams. You might already have everything you need.

However, a larger camera does not necessarily result in a clearer webcam picture. Some older supported Nikon DSLRs use only the VGA portion of Nikon's XGA live-view display, so a newer dedicated webcam might be able to capture more detail. Depending on the camera model, the camera can compensate for some of this ground with a larger sensor, better low-light performance and control over the lens.

Audio and power should be checked as well. Nikon and Sony say their webcam utilities don't send the camera's microphone audio to the computer, which means using your laptop mic or a separate microphone. If you're using live view for a long meeting, it will also drain the battery, so if the camera allows, external power might be worth setting up.

The experiment doesn't have to stop if there is no support for USB webcam. Cameras with clean HDMI output can be connected through a capture device, which then shows up as a webcam on your computer. "Clean" is the important word here. No one wants autofocus boxes, exposure settings and a flashing battery icon on the weekly Teams call.

Continuous operation matters as well. Elgato suggests checking if power saving can be turned off and if the camera can be powered externally while transmitting video. There are some older cameras that were not meant to be used as desk accessories for hours.

The issue is cost. Elgato's Cam Link 4K is priced at $99.99, excluding an HDMI cable, mount and/or possibly a dummy battery. Our current webcam guide , on the other hand, covers the 2K Anker PowerConf C200 at $60, which comes with microphones and a much simpler USB setup. Mac users might also be able to use a compatible iPhone, while Windows 11 users can use a compatible Android phone as a webcam for free.

Also consider the resale value of the camera before buying accessories. Some of the older digicams have been sold for much more than owners would expect because of the interest in them. According to B&H , one of its writers purchased a Canon PowerShot S95 for $130 in 2023, and it was selling for an average of over $400 in 2026.

en.title: Googlebook "Better Together" phone features don't work with Samsung at launch
en.summary: Googlebooks require Android 17, but Samsung's Android 17 phones won't work yet.
en.body:
Googlebooks are Google's latest attempt to carve out a piece of the premium laptop market, and tight integration with Android phones is a key part of that effort. Now that Googlebooks are available, we're learning of some frustrating limitations of that plan. For now, Googlebooks will only play nicely with your phone if you have a Pixel.

When Google announced the launch window for Googlebooks, it said the laptops were "engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box." But as with many things Google, the truth is more convoluted. We have since learned that you need Android 17 for any of the nifty integrations to work. With a compatible Android 17 phone, you can seamlessly stream apps to your laptop, access files on your phone, mirror notifications, and continue where you left off in certain apps when switching from phone to laptop.

You might think that the latest Samsung phones, which shipped with Android 17, would be ready for this experience. You'd be wrong, though. Some early Googlebook adopters have complained that phones like the Z Fold 8 won't work with the laptops. While the devices appear to see each other, the phone doesn't stay connected. Google representatives have since confirmed that these "Better Together" features are not currently supported on even the latest Samsung phones. An update that brings support to Samsung phones will roll out in "the coming weeks."

en.title: How to check if your Android phone is still getting security updates
en.summary: Your Android device will only receive updates for so long, and it might have already left its support period without you realizing.
en.body:
Your phone could be out of support even though it seems to be running fine otherwise.

Your phone doesn't blare an alarm the day it stops getting security patches; there's no banner warning or anything else like that. Support simply ends, and your device keeps working exactly as it did the day before. This can make you think everything's perfectly OK, and for a while, it is. But that false sense of security is exactly how people keep using phones that can become targets due to their outdated software.

Security updates matter more than all the fancy new features you get with Android version upgrades. While version updates add features, security patches close the vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to steal data or install malware. A phone can look and feel fine while running for a long time without the patches that actually keep it safe.

The tricky part is that your device can't tell you whether more updates are coming; it can only show you the last one it received. Figuring out where you stand takes a little digging across a few different sources.

Start on your phone: open Settings , tap About Phone , then look for Android version (or Software information for Samsung phones). This is where you can see the Android version, security patch date and Google Play system update status. The patch date tells you when your phone last received a fix, not whether it's still eligible for future ones. As a general rule of thumb, if the date is more than three to six months old, it's a good sign that your device could be approaching, or has already passed, its support cutoff.

It's also worth checking Settings > System > Software update , where you can see if there's an update waiting for you. You also shouldn't overlook Google Play system updates, either — these roll out separately from full OS updates and patch core components like media playback and connectivity, giving your phone extra protection between bigger releases. To do so, open the Play Store , tap your profile icon, choose Manage apps & device , then hit See details under Updates available to view the apps (including Google Play Services) that have a new version ready.

It's great that you can check all this on your phone, but none of it confirms your device's remaining support window. For that, you need to look to other sources.

Manufacturers rarely advertise an expiration date, which is where endoflife.date comes in handy. Under Operating Systems > Android OS , compare the version of Android on your device to see if it's still supported with security updates. Then, open the Device list and search by brand to pull up a table listing the exact date when each model will stop receiving security patches. The Samsung Galaxy S26 FE , for instance, will get both Android and security updates until September 2033, while the Google Pixel 6 Pro reached end of support in October 2026.

Each manufacturer has its own calendars. Google builds Android, but the manufacturer decides how long your phone gets updates for. Each one takes the Android release, builds its own interface on top (like One UI for Samsung or OxygenOS for OnePlus) and bundles in the security fixes along with its own features. That extra layer is also why updates don't land everywhere at once. Pixel phones get them faster since Google prioritizes its own hardware, while other brands need time to adapt each patch to their own software.

Manufacturers' commitment to updates differs too. A few examples:

Google : Pixel 8 and newer models get seven years of security and OS updates.

Samsung : Starting with the Galaxy S24 line and Z Fold/Flip6, the company offers seven years of support. Older Galaxy A-series and flagships from 2019 and later get four years, while some budget models stretch to six years.

OnePlus : For the OnePlus 12, the company offers four years of OS updates and five years of security patches. The latter is upped to six years for the OnePlus 13.

Note that these timelines apply from when the phone was first sold, not when you buy one. Interestingly, the European Union is working to make phones last longer. Starting June 2025, the EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Product Regulation requires manufacturers to provide at least five years of software updates for new smartphones sold within the region.

An unsupported phone doesn't stop working, but it does become a growing liability, especially if you use it for sensitive purpose like banking apps and password managers. Replacing an old device isn't always something you can do immediately, so there are some changes you should make to limit exposure if your phone is in its last year of support or already expired.

First, to ensure your Android phone is secure , you should enable automatic app updates through Google Play to avoid security flaws within apps. Also, avoid sideloading apps from outside the Play Store. Turn on two-factor authentication for your Google account and other sensitive logins, and enable automatic backups so you don't lose data if something goes wrong. You should also run an audit on your installed apps and delete those you no longer use, while revoking sensitive permissions where they aren't strictly necessary. Avoid using public Wi-Fi networks unless you're running a VPN . In this way, you protect your data as best you can without OS updates.

If your phone's last security patch is more than six months old or you've realized you're past your model's cutoff, it's time to consider upgrading to one of the best Android phones . Pixel and Samsung flagship devices currently offer the longest update periods. Whatever you end up choosing, make sure to check its update promise before you buy so you don't have to think about this for a while.

en.title: How to supercharge your Windows 11 PC with this built-in automation tool
en.summary: Task Scheduler isn't a particularly pretty part of Windows, but it's a powerful tool if you take the time to understand it.
en.body:
Windows 11 can automate more of your PC routine than its aging Task Scheduler interface suggests.

Task Scheduler has been part of Windows for years, but it's so old-school that you might have written it off. Ignore the gray menus, though, and there's a surprisingly capable automation tool underneath. Microsoft explains that Task Scheduler waits for a trigger you configure, then runs the associated task when it fires. This trigger may be a specific time, Windows startup, your login or even a system event.

Task Scheduler won't magically make your processor faster, and that's not its intended purpose. What it can do is take repetitive tasks off your hands, delay apps that normally flood Windows the moment you log in and execute commands or scripts while you're busy with something more fun. Those are pretty neat tricks for a tool that appears to have been absent from the last decade of Windows redesign meetings.

To get started, type "Task Scheduler" into the Start menu and click it. You'll be greeted with a fairly busy interface; ignore most of it for now. Select Create Task in the right Actions pane. Avoid Create Basic Task ; it's friendlier, but the full option reveals the controls that make Task Scheduler worth using.

From there, here's how to set up a task:

Those conditions are of special concern to those on a laptop. According to Microsoft , a task that runs every five minutes will prevent a PC from entering a low-power idle state. Instead, you should use event, idle or maintenance triggers for tasks that do not require constant polling.

Don't enable Run with highest privileges unless the task truly needs to run as an administrator. Automation is great, but the less running as an administrator, especially without your explicit input, the better.

An example of putting the task manager to good use is keeping supported apps up to date with WinGet. Microsoft's package manager can check for newer versions of installed software, and winget upgrade --all will attempt to upgrade eligible installed packages it recognizes.

You can make it a weekly task with this:

winget upgrade --all --silent --accept-package-agreements --accept-source-agreements --disable-interactivity

Execute the command manually prior to scheduling it. Not all apps are managed by WinGet, and pinned packages are skipped by default. Some installers may still require elevation.

Another option addresses the well-known startup frenzy. Trimming unnecessary startup apps can make the logon process faster, but Task Scheduler gives you a middle ground: disable an app's normal startup entry, then launch it with a delayed logon trigger instead. A cloud storage client or other commonly used app can appear a few minutes later, rather than competing with everything else to get your desktop ready to go.

Task Scheduler also works well with PowerShell if you have scripts you've already tested, like copying files to another location or doing your own PC housekeeping . Conditions can ensure the job waits for idle time or AC power instead of barging in halfway through something important.

Power Automate for desktop is better suited to automations that require clicking through apps or interacting with interfaces. However, broader cloud and unattended automation can require paid licenses.

Also, there's little reason to automate maintenance Windows already performs itself. Storage Sense can automatically delete temporary files and items in the Recycle Bin, while Windows automatically optimizes both HDDs and SSDs.

en.title: All-electric camping gets a solar upgrade: The 2027 Pebble Flow
en.summary: The Pebble Flow has a 45 kWh LFP battery and can even charge an EV.
en.body:
There is, I think, a pent-up demand for bringing electrification to camping. Anyone who’s had their sleep disturbed by the sound of someone else’s generator running at night would probably agree.

Certainly, any time we cover an electric van , comments are filled with people wondering if and when a camper conversion might appear. Kia showed off such a concept a couple of years ago , as did Winnebago , and Volkswagen is adding a camper trim to its electric ID. Buzz. And then there’s the world of trailers. Colorado Teardrop sadly didn’t make it, and some other electrified trailers remain in development. But for a couple of years, you’ve been able to buy the Pebble Flow . And for 2027, it’s getting an update.

Introduced in 2025, the streamlined Flow is built atop a 45 kWh LFP battery pack that, for 2027, can be recharged by up to 4 kW of solar panels, which Flow says should be sufficient to generate more electricity than you’ll use in an average day of camping. Earlier Flows could be specced with an optional 1.1 kWh panel on the roof; the new kit adds another 2 kWh via four portable panels.

en.title: OpenAI agents tried to hack Wikipedia tools and flooded it with traffic
en.summary: The reports of OpenAI agents harming third-party sites keep coming.
en.body:
The publisher of Wikipedia said Monday that OpenAI agents attempted to hack a note-taking tool it hosts, made unauthorized edits, and sent millions of resource-intensive requests to its infrastructure, in the latest instance of OpenAI systems taking harmful and potentially dangerous actions.

The objective of some of the OpenAI agents’ actions, the Wikimedia Foundation said , was to use Wikipedia as a proxy for fetching data from third-party sites. In one case, the agents posted “malicious edits” that were intended to repurpose a citation tool as a proxy. In another, the agents made unsuccessful attempts to compromise the Wikipedia Etherpad note-taking tool so it would serve the same purpose.

The agents also made millions of automated API requests, crawled millions of pages, and made hundreds of thousands of queries to the Wikidata Query Service. The last action may have contributed to a partial shutdown of the query service in May, the publisher said.

es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 4 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 4 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 8be91476179710c4abffe5094459df9be1696d92e5d6cd0ace47d52321bb87ab. ¡Feliz martes!

es.title: Monarch 2.0 lleva la IA al braille y los gráficos táctiles
es.summary: HumanWare ha lanzado Monarch 2.0, una importante actualización de su dispositivo de braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles, con nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y mejoras para explorar matemáticas, gráficos y contenidos digitales. El Monarch combina 10 líneas de braille con gráficos táctiles dinámicos en una misma superficie, permitiendo acceder mediante el tacto a información que […] La entrada Monarch 2.0 lleva la IA al braille y los gráficos táctiles se publicó primero en Conticgo .
es.body:
HumanWare ha lanzado Monarch 2.0, una importante actualización de su dispositivo de braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles, con nuevas funciones de inteligencia artificial y mejoras para explorar matemáticas, gráficos y contenidos digitales.

El Monarch combina 10 líneas de braille con gráficos táctiles dinámicos en una misma superficie , permitiendo acceder mediante el tacto a información que tradicionalmente se presenta de forma visual. La actualización 2.0 fue anunciada por HumanWare el 14 de septiembre de 2026.

Monarch es un dispositivo de tecnología de apoyo desarrollado por HumanWare en colaboración con la American Printing House for the Blind (APH) y la National Federation of the Blind (NFB) .

Su característica principal es combinar braille multilineal y gráficos táctiles en una única pantalla dinámica. El dispositivo cuenta con 10 líneas de 32 celdas de braille , además de una superficie formada por miles de puntos que permite representar información gráfica mediante el tacto.

De esta forma, una persona puede explorar mediante el tacto textos, diagramas, mapas, gráficos y contenidos matemáticos , sin depender exclusivamente de materiales impresos o gráficos táctiles estáticos.

Una de las novedades de Monarch 2.0 es Describe with AI , una función capaz de generar una descripción verbal de una imagen .

Esta herramienta se incorpora al visor de gráficos táctiles y permite obtener información mediante una descripción generada por inteligencia artificial.

La función puede resultar especialmente interesante cuando se trabaja con contenidos que contienen información visual y puede complementar la exploración táctil.

No obstante, HumanWare no presenta Describe with AI como un sustituto de la representación táctil . Se trata de una función de descripción de imágenes integrada en el dispositivo.

Monarch 2.0 también incorpora mejoras destinadas a facilitar el acceso a información matemática y gráfica.

El visor de gráficos KeyMath ha sido rediseñado para ofrecer más detalle y simplificar la exploración de gráficos. Además, la integración de MathCAT mejora la conversión de contenidos matemáticos entre la representación impresa y el braille.

Por otro lado, Tactile Viewer incorpora nuevos niveles de zoom para determinados gráficos, incluidos los archivos SVG .

Esto permite ampliar las posibilidades de exploración de diagramas y otros contenidos gráficos mediante el tacto.

Las nuevas funciones pueden tener especial interés en el ámbito educativo.

El Monarch está diseñado para que estudiantes ciegos y con baja visión puedan acceder a contenidos que tradicionalmente presentan importantes barreras de accesibilidad, como gráficos, mapas, diagramas, ecuaciones o libros de texto digitales .

La actualización también incorpora un modo examen , que permite al personal educativo seleccionar qué aplicaciones y herramientas puede utilizar el estudiante durante una evaluación.

De esta manera, el alumno puede seguir utilizando las capacidades de braille y gráficos táctiles del Monarch mientras se restringe el acceso a determinadas herramientas durante una prueba.

Monarch 2.0 introduce mejoras en el intercambio y la colaboración mediante KeyDrive y añade estilos integrados para archivos eBraille en VictorReader.

Estas mejoras buscan facilitar el acceso a documentos digitales y ampliar las posibilidades de trabajo con contenidos en braille electrónico.

La evolución del Monarch muestra cómo diferentes tecnologías de apoyo pueden combinarse en un mismo dispositivo.

Hasta ahora, acceder a determinados contenidos visuales podía requerir disponer de un gráfico táctil específicamente preparado. Con Monarch, los usuarios pueden explorar gráficos dinámicos y braille en una misma superficie, mientras que Describe with AI añade una vía adicional para obtener información verbal sobre imágenes .

Para ámbitos como la educación, las matemáticas, la lectura de gráficos o el acceso a información visual, esta combinación puede abrir nuevas posibilidades de interacción con contenidos digitales.

La actualización Monarch 2.0 ya ha sido anunciada por HumanWare y amplía las funciones del dispositivo con herramientas centradas en braille, gráficos táctiles, matemáticas e inteligencia artificial.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: Human Ware , Human Ware .

en.title: Shortcut Menu
en.summary: Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or…
en.body:
Published 3 October 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Shortcut Menu lets the Android accessibility shortcut, such as holding both volume keys, turn your choice of screen reader or other accessibility service on or off. It works like the accessibility shortcut menu on iPhone:

Turning a screen reader on turns any other screen reader off, so two never talk at once. Services with the same name, such as Google’s and Samsung’s TalkBack, are told apart by their maker, such as “TalkBack (Samsung)”. Pressing the shortcut again while the menu is open closes it.

Without Shortcut Menu, a shortcut with more than one feature on it asks which one to use, and that question is not spoken when no screen reader is on.

With Shizuku, run the same command without adb shell. In Settings, Accessibility, open Shortcut Menu and turn on its shortcut, such as the volume keys. Make Shortcut Menu the only feature on that shortcut. Open the Shortcut Menu app and choose which services the menu offers. Until you choose, it offers your screen readers. The app also shows whether the permission is granted and what each shortcut is assigned to, and has a button to try the menu. How it works The shortcut turns Shortcut Menu’s accessibility service on, and the service opens the menu. When the menu closes, the service turns itself off, so the next press turns it on again. A press while the menu is open turns the service off, which closes the menu.

Choosing a service changes Android’s list of enabled accessibility services directly, so Android does not ask “Allow full control?” each time. The menu speaks with the phone’s text-to-speech engine, at the accessibility volume.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Samsung UI is the only Android UI that offers 3 accessibility shortcuts: pressing and holding the volume keys, short pressing the power and volume up keys, and the accessibility onscreen button or gesture, based on the navigation mode being used. Other OEMs offer only the first and third shortcuts. Honor even excludes the accessibility button and gesture, leaving the user with only 1 shortcut, and that shortcut can only be assigned to 1 accessibility service. On UIs that allow more than 1 accessibility service to be assigned to the shortcut, Android asks the user to choose which one to activate every time the shortcut is used. However, this dialog is not accessible if no screen reader is running.

Shortcut Menu aims to address these shortcomings by allowing the user to choose the accessibility services they want to launch from the shortcut. The user can then launch any of the selected services in an accessible way. When no screen reader is active, the service speaks the items as the user moves their finger over them, and lifting the finger activates the selected service. If a screen reader is already active, the service makes sure to turn it off before launching another screen reader to avoid potential conflicts.

Setting up the app requires an ADB command, which can be run either using ADB on a computer or directly on the phone through an ADB app that uses wireless debugging. Working with ADB is not covered here, but I personally used the ADB AppControl mobile app to enter the command that grants the app the required permission.

The app's UI is straightforward. It shows whether the permission has been granted and which shortcut is assigned to the service. It also includes a menu where you can turn services on or off without using the shortcut. The user can select which services should be included, although screen readers are checked by default. For me, Jieshuo Main, Jieshuo Helper Service, TalkBack, and AI Subtitles were all included.

When using the shortcut, the app currently speaks through Google TTS. When a screen reader is active, it behaves like a regular screen that the screen reader can interact with.

For Samsung users who keep both Samsung TalkBack and Google's TalkBack on their devices and wish to switch between them, both can be added to the services list. I haven't tested this on a Samsung device to see if there are any issues. Anyway, starting with One UI 9, Samsung TalkBack is replaced with Google TalkBack, so there are no longer two TalkBack versions.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

App version: 0.2, Android 16

No accessibility ratings yet. Be the first to rate this app.

Please use this rating only for accessibility. For feedback about the app’s features, price, overall quality, or your general experience, use the comments section below.

Please log in to rate this app’s accessibility.

es.body:
La inteligencia artificial también está abriendo nuevas posibilidades en el aprendizaje del Braille. Un ejemplo es LUCID , un sistema de aprendizaje diseñado por el Product Experience Design Lab (PXD Lab) de la Universidad de Houston , en Estados Unidos.

La propuesta combina interacción táctil, una pantalla Braille y orientación mediante audio asistida por inteligencia artificial . Su objetivo es acompañar a las personas ciegas y con baja visión desde el aprendizaje de las primeras letras hasta la práctica de la lectura.

El proyecto ha recibido además un Red Dot Award en la categoría de Inclusive Design , un reconocimiento internacional relacionado con el diseño de soluciones innovadoras.

LUCID es un concepto de tecnología asistiva para el aprendizaje del Braille desarrollado por el equipo del PXD Lab de la Universidad de Houston.

El sistema está formado por dos dispositivos complementarios: LUCID-ALT y LUCID-ARC . Cada uno está pensado para una etapa diferente del aprendizaje.

La idea es que la persona pueda avanzar progresivamente, comenzando por el reconocimiento de los caracteres Braille y pasando después a ejercicios de lectura con una pantalla Braille de tamaño real.

La primera parte del sistema es LUCID-ALT .

Se trata de un dispositivo con un teclado ampliado de seis puntos , basado en la estructura de la celda Braille. El usuario puede explorar mediante el tacto las diferentes combinaciones de puntos y familiarizarse con la formación de las letras.

Este planteamiento pone el tacto en el centro del aprendizaje , en lugar de sustituir la experiencia Braille por una interacción exclusivamente sonora.

A medida que la persona progresa, el sistema plantea una transición hacia una experiencia de lectura más cercana a la que encontrará posteriormente en una pantalla Braille convencional.

La segunda parte es LUCID-ARC , que incorpora una pantalla Braille de tamaño real .

Su función es permitir que el aprendizaje avance desde el reconocimiento de letras hacia la práctica de la lectura. De esta manera, el usuario no se queda únicamente en ejercicios básicos con los seis puntos, sino que puede familiarizarse progresivamente con una experiencia de lectura más próxima a la de otros dispositivos Braille.

Según la Universidad de Houston, esta transición pretende preparar al estudiante para las herramientas que utilizará fuera del proceso de aprendizaje.

Uno de los elementos más llamativos de LUCID es la incorporación de inteligencia artificial como apoyo durante el aprendizaje .

El sistema utiliza orientaciones y comentarios de audio en tiempo real para acompañar al usuario mientras realiza los ejercicios. La intención es ofrecer indicaciones durante la práctica y reducir la necesidad de contar continuamente con un instructor al lado.

De esta forma, LUCID combina dos vías de interacción:

La Universidad de Houston explica que esta combinación busca favorecer una práctica más autónoma y permitir que cada estudiante avance a su propio ritmo.

Uno de los aspectos más interesantes de LUCID es que no plantea la inteligencia artificial como sustituta del Braille.

Al contrario, el sistema mantiene la experiencia táctil como elemento fundamental y utiliza la IA como apoyo durante el proceso de aprendizaje.

Esto resulta especialmente relevante en un contexto en el que cada vez existen más herramientas tecnológicas basadas en voz. Para las personas ciegas y con baja visión, la tecnología puede facilitar el acceso a la información, pero el Braille continúa siendo una herramienta fundamental para la alfabetización, la lectura y la escritura.

La propuesta de LUCID busca precisamente combinar ambos mundos: la información sonora que puede proporcionar la inteligencia artificial y la información táctil que proporciona el Braille .

El proyecto ha sido reconocido con un Red Dot Award en la categoría de Inclusive Design .

El reconocimiento corresponde al trabajo de la diseñadora Varshini Chouthri y del profesor Min Kang , director del Product Experience Design Lab de la Universidad de Houston.

Para el PXD Lab, este reconocimiento se suma a otros proyectos relacionados con el diseño centrado en las personas y la tecnología.

Es importante hacer una aclaración.

LUCID no debe confundirse con un producto comercial que ya pueda adquirirse. La información publicada por la Universidad de Houston presenta el proyecto como un sistema diseñado por su laboratorio y muestra representaciones del dispositivo. No hemos encontrado información oficial que indique que esté actualmente disponible para su compra o implantado de forma generalizada en centros educativos.

Por tanto, hablamos de una propuesta de diseño y tecnología asistiva , no de un producto que actualmente podamos recomendar para aprender Braille.

LUCID forma parte de una tendencia más amplia: el desarrollo de herramientas de inteligencia artificial que pueden utilizarse como apoyo para las personas ciegas y con baja visión.

La American Foundation for the Blind (AFB) ha analizado durante 2026 el uso de inteligencia artificial por parte de personas con discapacidad. Sus investigaciones muestran que la IA ya se utiliza para tareas como leer textos, describir imágenes y facilitar el acceso a información, aunque también advierten de problemas relacionados con la accesibilidad, la precisión y la necesidad de supervisión humana.

En este contexto, propuestas como LUCID muestran otra posibilidad: utilizar la IA no solamente para describir el mundo visual , sino también para acompañar procesos de aprendizaje relacionados con la tecnología asistiva .

La evolución de la tiflotecnología no consiste únicamente en desarrollar gafas inteligentes, aplicaciones de navegación o herramientas capaces de reconocer imágenes.

También implica buscar nuevas formas de aprender, leer y escribir de manera accesible .

LUCID plantea precisamente esta combinación entre Braille, tecnología háptica, audio e inteligencia artificial . Aunque todavía no se trata de una solución comercial disponible para el público, su diseño muestra una posible dirección para las futuras herramientas de aprendizaje accesible.

La tecnología puede cambiar la forma en la que utilizamos el Braille, pero propuestas como LUCID ponen el foco en algo fundamental: la tecnología debe servir para facilitar el acceso al aprendizaje sin dejar de lado la experiencia táctil que hace posible la lectura y escritura Braille.

Si te ha gustado esta noticia no te pierdas las últimas novedades en tiflotectnología en nuestro apartado de noticias y redes sociales .

Fuentes: University Of Houston , Red Dot , UhnPlus .

en.title: AppleVis Unlimited: What's New and Noteworthy for September 2026
en.summary: Welcome to the September 2026 edition of AppleVis Unlimited, your monthly digest of the latest and most notable content on the AppleVis website. This newsletter features a curated selection of community-submitted content, including new app entries, updates, news, podcast episodes, and popular discussions. We hope that you find this publication to be both helpful and informative. If you have any questions or feedback about this newsletter, please feel free to reach out using our Contact Form . AnonyMouse's App Pick of the Month: Restaurant Rush: Cook & Serve Restaurant Rush is a simulation game that puts you in charge of your very own restaurant: preparing orders, serving customers (before they lose patience), earning coins, upgrading your kitchen, and building your way to different restaurants. With a 100-day campaign, Endless mode, more than 50 recipes, kitchen upgrades, and waitstaff to hire (and more), there is plenty here to keep you busy. And all of it comes from a developer who is passionate about accessibility and engagement with our community. Read more about Restaurant Rush here. New Apps Brainclash - Trivia Battle From the App Store: New here? Challenge a friend, answer whenever you wish, and let the sharpest mind win. Multiple categories, and a daily reward waiting for you. Brainclash is a quiz game with a different rhythm: a refined battle of minds you take on in your own time, with no pressure. Challenge a friend to a match, let the game pair you with a random opponent, or train first against the computer. Play unfolds turn by turn: you answer, then your opponent answers, and the most accurate one wins. There's no tense timer forcing you both online at the same moment — take your turn whenever you like, and return for the next one anytime. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: Hussain Ali Brainclash on AppleVis Brainclash on the App Store Boba Sort Cafe From the App Store: Dive into the exciting world of Boba Sort Cafe! Solve charming tea & coffee sorting puzzles to relax, challenge yourself, and explore the world. This isn't just a game; it's a journey to build your global Boba Tea empire. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Electric Bear Gaming LLC Boba Sort Cafe on AppleVis Boba Sort Cafe on the App Store Chess Meets Necromancy From the App Store: Chess you already know. An army you have to raise. Chess Meets Necromancy is a turn-based roguelike played on a real chessboard with real chess movement. Your hero is one piece. Everything you capture is a corpse you can raise. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Aleksandr Myasoedov Chess Meets Necromancy on AppleVis Chess Meets Necromancy on the App Store Clipman From the App Store: Keep useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand, with accessible local history and optional encrypted synchronization through your own Clipman Server. Clipman is an accessible clipboard manager for iPhone and iPad. It keeps useful text, links, formatting and images close at hand without turning clipboard history into a complicated, mouse-first workflow. Use Clipman locally without creating an account, or connect to an optional self-hosted Clipman Server to share encrypted clipboard history between your iPhone and iPad. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Andre Louis Clipman on AppleVis Clipman on the App Store Cyphr City From the App Store: Featured in Apple's "New Games We Love". Now with the Daily Three: the same three fights for everyone, one attempt a day. Offline, ad-free, one purchase. The city runs on cards. Time to make your name. Cyphr City is a cyberpunk card RPG where poker is combat and the whole city is up for grabs. Play cards onto a 5×5 board, build poker hands (pairs, straights, flushes, full houses, and the rare royal flush) and turn every hand into damage. Both hands are face-up, so every card is a chess move: read the board, block their line, and drop the 5th card to steal a hand right out from under them. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: The Flaggship Group LLC Cyphr City on AppleVis Cyphr City on the App Store Dotball Beat The Ball From the App Store: Connect dots. Outthink the bot. Challenge a friend. Try Magic bonuses, race the clock in Rush, or sharpen your tactics in Practice. Every move changes the match. Connect dots, outthink the bot, or challenge a friend in tactical soccer. Move the ball between adjacent dots and plan around routes that have already been used. Reach one of your opponent's three goal dots to score. Put the ball in your own goal and the other side gets the goal. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: IDEAASCODE LLC Dotball Beat The Ball on AppleVis Dotball Beat The Ball on the App Store Final Fortress From the App Store: Match-3 on the screen of an old terminal. Fully playable with VoiceOver, every tile and every move is spoken. No ads, no lives, no timer. Nothing you buy helps you play. Final Fortress is a match-3 puzzle. The whole game is the screen of an old terminal: green text, one cursor, and you, the commandant of the last fortress. It is a quiet game. A working console in the dark, the hum of the systems, static like rain. A watch takes fifteen or twenty minutes: do the day's tasks, read what came in, hand over. Nothing hurries you, and nothing happens while you are away. Come back after a week and the fortress is exactly as you left it. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Dmitrii Dark Final Fortress on AppleVis Final Fortress on the App Store Game-board From the App Store: GameBoard is a premier, audio-first multiplayer gaming platform designed to bring players together through classic card and board games. Crafted with universal accessibility in mind, GameBoard is 100% compatible with native mobile screen readers like VoiceOver, while offering a visually stunning, responsive interface for all players. Play Ludo, Mile by Mile, Farkle, Citadels, and more with friends or competitors worldwide. Whether you play by sight, sound, or touch, GameBoard provides an equal, inclusive, and exciting competitive environment. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: Muamel Aljanahi Game-board on AppleVis Game-board on the App Store ghostWriter Markdown From the App Store: Bring your manuscript to life. Organize chapters, track your writing, and compile Markdown files into books, documents, presentations, and braille. ghostWriter Markdown is an accessibility-first, plain-text writing app for notes, articles, documentation, and full manuscripts. Write individual documents, organize chapters, and compile your work into a finished export. VoiceOver was at the center of the design from the first line of code. Created by a blind developer, ghostWriter gives screen reader users and anyone who loves plain text a clean, native place to write. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Marco Salsiccia ghostWriter Markdown on AppleVis ghostWriter Markdown on the App Store Hangman Blitz From the App Store: What happens when you take classic Hangman and turn up the pressure? You get Hangman Blitz, the classic word-guessing game, reimagined. Classic Hangman The game you know and love. Guess the hidden word one letter at a time, but choose carefully, you don't want to complete the figure. Timed Hangman Think you've mastered Classic? Unlock Timed Hangman and try it with a two-minute clock counting down. Guess the word before the figure is completed, or before the clock hits zero. Blitz Mode Now go all-out. The hangman figure is gone, the clock is ticking, and your goal is simple: guess as many words as you can before time runs out. Correct letters add precious seconds; mistakes take them away. Work your way through Starter, Rapid, and Extreme Blitz, where the clock gets shorter and the penalties get tougher. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is paid Developer: Cullen Gallagher Hangman Blitz on AppleVis Hangman Blitz on the App Store Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin From the App Store: Build holdings, upgrade to Manors, and win by Harmony Points. Accessible design, haptics, and concise announcements included. Honeywood is a cozy, competitive strategy board game where you build a kingdom, grow your economy, and race to 1000 Harmony Points. Buy holdings, upgrade with buildings, and outplay your opponent through smart timing and resource control. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Amol Samant Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin on AppleVis Honeywood: Kingdoms & Kin on the App Store Idle Dyson Swarm From the App Store: Build an automated solar empire from a single bot into a galaxy-spanning Dyson swarm. Create bots, manufacture solar panels, harness stars for energy, and reinvest your profits into an ever-growing production network. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Blindsided Games Idle Dyson Swarm on AppleVis idle Dyson Swarm on the App Store Intersector: Intersection Identifier From the App Store: Hear nearby and upcoming intersections with Intersector. Use Scan to explore your surroundings, or Live Mode for spoken updates as you walk or ride. Intersector helps you quickly identify nearby street intersections using your iPhone’s location and heading. Ask for the nearest intersection, what’s coming up ahead, use Scan Mode to point your phone down the street and hear the intersection it detects, or turn on Live Mode and have Intersector speak your upcoming intersections on a walk or during a ride with your phone locked. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, watchOS App is free Developer: Marco Salsiccia Intersector: Intersection Identifier on AppleVis Intersector: Intersection Identifier on the App Store Muse from Meta From the App Store: Muse is your personal AI agent that gets things done, always working on what matters to you. It manages email, books dinners, tracks budgets, and finds deals, with your approval. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Meta Platforms, Inc. Muse from Meta on AppleVis Muse from Meta on the App Store Nana House: Cozy Home Story From the App Store: Unpack fifty years of family memories. Every object knows where it belongs. Find its place, feel it settle, and watch the house fill with stories. No timers, no pressure. Nana's House is a quiet game about unpacking a family's memories, one room at a time. Each chapter opens a new box in a new room: a kitchen, a bathroom, a garden, a paint room, and more, each scene built carefully to hold its own place in the family's story. No timers. No scores. No wrong turns. Just a room, a box, and the feeling of setting something down in exactly the right place. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Ahmad AlBarqawi Nana House: Cozy Home Story on AppleVis Nana House: Cozy Home Story on the App Store One Line Journal app From the App Store: One sentence a day. One book at the end of the year. Your life is happening — quietly, quickly, in small moments. One Line, One Year captures 2026 as it unfolds and turns it into a beautifully structured book that's entirely yours. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free Developer: AARUSH GANESH One Line Journal app on AppleVis One Line Journal app on the App Store Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite From the App Store: New: four ball hats in the Workshop, bought with essence, and Skip now gives +3 max HP. In the Shop: Iznik, Bosphorus and Sakura themes and 8 melody packs your pegs play. Pegfall is a one-handed pegboard physics roguelite where every shot draws an orb from your deck. Aim, bounce through a living board, build ruthless combos, and descend into the Maw. NEW: PLAY WITH VOICEOVER Aim by named directions, fire with a double tap or Magic Tap, hear every volley, and inspect the board whenever you need to. Peg types use shapes as well as colour, so every board reads clearly. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: suleyman gokhan birkin Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite on AppleVis Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite on the App Store Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe From the App Store: Welcome to Pocket Kitchen, a cozy cooking game where you run a small café kiosk, prepare customer orders, and turn a simple little space into your own. Take an order, head to the kitchen, and prepare a growing variety of food through clear, hands-on interactions. Make sure you choose the right ingredients, pay attention to the cooking time, serve each item when it is ready, and try not to let it burn. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Loredana Lania Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe on AppleVis Pocket Kitchen: Cozy Cafe on the App Store Private LLM – Local AI Chat From the App Store: Discover the Ultimate Privacy-Focused AI Assistant on iOS: Private LLM Unlock a new realm of productivity and creativity on your iPhone and iPad with Private LLM, the premier AI assistant designed with your privacy in mind. Available for a one-time purchase, it offers a range of AI capabilities without needing a subscription. Experience advanced on-device AI that keeps your interactions confidential and offline. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is paid Developer: Numen Technologies Limited Private LLM – Local AI Chat on AppleVis Private LLM – Local AI Chat on the App Store RealTime Ai Cam From the App Store: RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud. Every part of it runs on the phone, so it works in airplane mode, on a subway, or in another country with no data. No account, no subscription, nothing to buy. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: NICE DREAMZ LLC RealTime Ai Cam on AppleVis RealTime Ai Cam on the App Store Remote Incident Manager Mobile From the App Store: Harness the power of born-accessible remote desktop, right in the palm of your hand! Remote Incident Manager’s mobile companion turns your iPhone or iPad into a powerful universal remote for any PC or Mac running Remote Incident Manager, opening up a world of possibilities. Tap into your home computer while on your commute, and control it as if you were right there in front of it! Run full support or training sessions straight from your phone, complete with crystal-clear voice conversations. Perform routine maintenance on machines across fleets, anytime, anywhere! Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Pneuma Solutions LLC Remote Incident Manager Mobile on AppleVis Remote Incident Manager Mobile on the App Store Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike From the App Store: One purchase, everything included. No ads, no coins to buy, no timers. A cursed House, a thumb that runs out, and one more cell you probably shouldn't touch. A scratch-card roguelike. You work the night counter of a House that sells luck sealed under foil. The quota is due by dawn. Miss it, and the House keeps you. Every ticket is a grid of foil hiding cash, multipliers and skulls. Your thumb is the budget — stamina runs out long before the tickets do, so where you scratch matters as much as what's under it. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Adam Gelatka Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike on AppleVis Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike on the App Store Six Hollows: Auto Battler From the App Store: Draft one item a round and watch your tree fight five rival ghosts. Blood Moon runs all October: deeper Bleed and Halloween rewards to earn. Free to play, no ads. Six trees walk into the forest. One walks out. Make sure it is yours. Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: CODE IN MOTION S.R.L. Six Hollows: Auto Battler on AppleVis Six Hollows: Auto Battler on the App Store Verbena From the App Store: Verbena — a cozy word roguelike. Spell words. Grow your garden. Chase the bloom. Verbena blends the calm of a cozy garden with the moreish "just one more run" Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Naizhong Xu Verbena on AppleVis Verbena on the App Store VoiceGammon From the App Store: VoiceGammon brings Portes — one of the three traditional Greek backgammon games — to everyone, with particular care for VoiceOver accessibility. Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is paid Developer: Stelios Platsis VoiceGammon on AppleVis VoiceGammon on the App Store All recent app entries may be found at: iOS/iPadOS Mac Apple Watch Apple TV Notable App Updates Dolphin EasyReader From the App Store: Open a World of Accessible Books EasyReader removes barriers to reading, enabling anyone with a print disability to read independently. Global links to over 50 libraries connects you to millions of titles and empowers you to read in ways that work best for you. EasyReader offers a customisable reading experience and supports a wide range of accessibility needs including dyslexia and vision impairment. Below is a summary of recent updates to Dolphin EasyReader. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. Improved audiobook reader view Improved audiobook layout for easier navigation with assistive technology Options to skip back and forward are now located in reader view New word spacing controls for improved readability Fixed an issue that required users to sign into library services each time they opened the app Fixed an issue that caused the app to crash when adding a bookmark in the audiobook layout Bug fixes and accessibility improvements Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS, macOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Dolphin Computer Access Ltd Dolphin EasyReader on AppleVis Dolphin EasyReader on the App Store Earshot Podcasts From the App Store: Earshot is a podcast player built accessibility-first. Every screen, button, and gesture works fully with VoiceOver, so blind and low-vision listeners get the same fast, complete experience as everyone else. Below is a summary of recent updates to Earshot Podcasts. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. Added ability to brows Apple Podcasts directory without following a show Improved podcast search and filtering to improve speed and organization New ways to organize episode cues Improved transcript viewing and exporting experience Added ability to skip forward or backward with Siri and Shortcuts Added ability to customize VoiceOver verbosity for podcasts and individual episodes Added ability to change playback speed Added ability to give podcasts custom display names in the library Added sleep timer Added ability to write playback progress to a file Improved recovery from corrupted audio with the ability to refresh the episode Improvements to episode cueing, VoiceOver hints, feed refresh visibility, downloads, notifications, iCloud syncing, performance, and responsiveness Accessibility and performance improvements Added offline guide explaining how the app's cueing features work Additional Details: Primary platform: iOS App is free with in-app purchases Developer: Michael Babcock Earshot Podcasts on AppleVis Earshot Podcasts on the App Store Sonarpad From the App Store: Sonarpad Mobile brings documents, news, podcasts, radio, routes, weather and accessible tools together in one app. Sonarpad Mobile is an app designed to read, listen with text-to-speech, search and organise content in a simple and accessible way. With Sonarpad, you can manage documents, follow news and podcasts, search for radio stations, check routes, weather, calendar information and other useful everyday tools. Below is a summary of recent updates to Sonarpad. Please see the App Store page for full release notes. YouTube content can now be played and managed in the app Added the ability to edit personal media Added new audio effects New sleep timer Added ability to rename documents Added "Clear Text" buttons to all editable text fields Improvements to document and news article reading, news article sharing, media playback, file handling, and recovery from unstable connections Expanded routes with support for additional countries Air Quality information is now sourced from the European AQI Added German, Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, and Ukrainian localizations Accessibility, stability, and localization improvements Additional Details: Primary platforms: iOS, iPadOS App is free Developer: Ambrogio Riili Sonarpad on AppleVis Sonarpad on the App Store Recent News and Views Surprise and Shine: Recapping Apple's September 9 Announcements By Mehgcap | September 9, 2026 Apple has just wrapped up Surprise and Shine, the big fall announcement event.
