en.title: Google Is Rolling Out Guided Vision to Gemini Live: Here’s How to Use It and My Early Impressions
en.summary: Google allows users to turn on the camera feed while in a conversation with Gemini Live, so they can ask about things that are in…
en.body:
Published 23 September 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Google allows users to turn on the camera feed while in a conversation with Gemini Live, so they can ask about things that are in view. Although a blind user can take advantage of this feature, it is not designed specifically to assist blind people. Google is now rolling out Guided vision, a mode that uses the camera in a live conversation to help blind people get an overview of their surroundings, read text, and more. This post covers turning the feature on and using it, as well as my first impressions from testing it.

Note that I haven’t done anything special to access Guided vision on my Honor 600 Pro, but I am running a three-month AI Pro trial that came as an offer with my device, so I don’t know if that affected the feature’s arrival on my device. The feature is not available for my other Accessible Android colleagues yet.

Table of Contents

To enable Guided vision:

A notification appears on the screen with the ability to start a Live session directly. When you use the button to start the Live session, it starts with the camera feed enabled, so you can start talking.

Note that the feature is still not available for everyone, so you should wait if you cannot find the Guided vision toggle in Settings.

According to the Google Accessibility help article , it’s possible to assign Guided vision to an accessibility shortcut, and you can launch it through TalkBack too. However, both are still not available on my device. In fact, I haven’t received any TalkBack update recently.

I haven’t tested to see if launching the camera in a Live conversation when Guided vision is active uses the mode without any user’s intervention, but during my tests, I always asked Gemini to start Guided vision to make sure that it works in that mode. When I tried to prompt the assistant to start the feature, it asked me to point the camera at what I wanted described, but that was one of its hallucinations, as it didn’t open the camera feed or start the Live conversation. Starting a Live conversation is still necessary.

At another time, I asked it to start a Live conversation with Guided vision, but at that instance, it told me that it couldn’t start it automatically and asked me to start Live manually.

Note that turning off Guided vision and then turning it back on from Settings shows the notification to start a Live conversation again, which can be used to start a conversation with the camera turned on.

When I had my first conversation with Live with Guided vision turned on, Gemini reminded me that it cannot detect all hazards or guarantee path clearance and that I should use my mobility aid before almost every response. I kept telling it that I understand the risks and that it shouldn’t repeat those warnings. During the later conversations, I didn’t hear any of the warnings. I am not sure, though, if my early prompting helped, or if you hear those warnings only during the first conversation to alert you of the risks or when Gemini thinks that it should do so for your safety.

During conversations with Guided vision active, I couldn’t find any indication that a special mode is active. All Live-related controls are the same, with no difference. However, the difference is in how Gemini acts. During my short tests, I found that Gemini tried to be detailed in its descriptions because it was aware that Guided vision is active and that the mode is designed to assist blind users.

I was able to ask it questions about the mode, and I got assurance from it that the mode is to assist blind users. It gave me guidance on how to move the camera to show certain objects or scenes better. When I asked it to tell me how to move to reach something, it told me that it needed to know exactly where I was in relation to the camera’s orientation. Using my hand as a reference, it gave me directions with respect to my hand. It also described the positions of items in the room relative to each other, like the position of a fan relative to the sofa.

Additionally, Gemini told me the book that I was holding and tried to assist me in putting the full page in view. When I asked it to read the page, it read a part of the page, though. However, when I asked it if that was the only text on the page, it correctly stated that there were other texts and visual diagrams and offered to describe them for me.

These observations are based on my initial tests, and I haven’t made direct comparisons between using Guided vision with the feature turned on and using the normal Live camera mode with it turned off.

Guided vision changes only how Gemini tries to provide information, as well as making it give more hints to assist a blind user. However, it is still a part of the Live experience. This means that current Live limitations are still present. The most important limitation is the need to prompt it again to tell you about any change, as Live doesn’t have real-time monitoring or continuous picture analysis capabilities.

Another factor worth mentioning is the model used, as Guided vision doesn’t switch Gemini to a more capable AI model than the one that you are using in your Gemini app.

Although image analysis has already advanced and helps in many scenarios, misidentifications are always a part of the formula that shouldn’t be forgotten. For example, a towel hanging on a door was identified more than once as pink, although it wasn’t pink.

Additionally, leveraging the new mode to take pictures still needs work. After Gemini gave me directions to centre my face and I told it to take a photo, it obeyed my order, opened the camera, and took a photo, but that led to the termination of the Live session. That behavior ended the conversation without being able to make sure that the photo was properly captured or without asking any additional questions about what it includes.

Guided vision is an interesting step forward from Google in tailoring Live camera to blind users. Although Google still has the Lookout app , it decided to make Guided vision a part of the Gemini app. Google decided to launch the feature and mention TalkBack as one of the methods to turn it on before releasing a TalkBack update that includes the necessary shortcut. There is even no accessibility service that can be assigned to an accessibility shortcut at the time of writing. However, an interesting thing for users who rely on other screen readers is that using the feature is not tied to having TalkBack running. I am almost sure that Gemini doesn’t check whether a screen reader is running as a requirement to use the feature.

Although it is in its early stages, I am excited to keep Guided vision on, and I am not considering going back to the normal camera mode. This should minimize the need to remind Gemini that I am blind or to try to speak prompts asking it to help me guide my camera toward the subject I am asking about or the text I want it to help me read.

Google doesn’t lack the resources to improve how Guided vision works, with the money and ability to make Gemini Live a trusted assistant, as much as “trusted” can be used with AI services, that understands the needs of blind people and helps them live a more independent life.

Published in Reviews Tutorials

en.title: Scratch Mancer: Card Roguelike
en.summary: A scratch-card roguelike. You work the night counter of a House that sells luck sealed under foil. The quota is due by dawn. Miss it, and the House keeps you. Every ticket is a grid of foil hiding cash, multipliers and skulls. Your thumb is the budget — stamina runs out long before the tickets do, so where you scratch matters as much as what's under it. THE DECISION YOU MAKE ALL GAME • Scratch a cell to 20% and you can read the fragment — it doesn't count and it doesn't trigger • Scratch to 45% and it counts for real, skulls included • One revealed skull halves the payout. Two void the ticket • Cash out whenever you like. Only what you revealed pays BUILD A RUN THAT BENDS THE ODDS • 40 charms across 5 slots: reroll skulls into coins, drift sevens toward corners, make a graze count as a hit • A warden calls every third night. Each one bends a rule you were leaning on. There are six of them • Seven ticket types, each with its own payout rule — match three, complete a crossword, climb a rising ladder, or reveal a single cell on an Offering and stop • Four single-use tools in three pockets: spray the foil to see straight through it, magnet a symbol sideways, sticker a skull into a seven • Nine nights, each with a quota due at dawn. Then endless, if you're still standing • Beat the House and the Seals open: seven stacked terms for the players who won, one added per win. Higher quotas, a skull on every ticket, wardens arriving early, two on the last night. Break all seven NO ADS. NO PAYWALLS. JUST SCRATCHING. One purchase, the whole game. The odds don't know what you paid, because there is no second payment to make: no coins to buy, no subscription, no season pass, no timers. • Plays fully offline • Family Sharing enabled • Game Center achievements and leaderboards • One thumb, portrait, a night finishes on a bus ride • Built for iPhone and iPad by one developer Scratch the foil, read what you can, and try to leave before the House notices. Scratchmancer is a work of fiction. No real money changes hands, no real lottery products appear, and the odds in it are invented.

en.title: Chess Meets Necromancy
en.summary: Chess you already know. An army you have to raise. Chess Meets Necromancy is a turn-based roguelike played on a real chessboard with real chess movement. Your hero is one piece. Everything you capture is a corpse you can raise. THE RUN Twenty waves across four acts. Enemies move like the pieces they are - grunts step like pawns, lancers leap like knights, imp matrons slide like queens. Clear the board, take a relic, spend your gold, march on. Die and the run is over. RAISE AN ARMY Spend souls next to your hero to raise Skeletons, Bone Knights, Wraiths, Bone Golems and Seraphs. Every summon moves as a chess piece. Give them a stance - Hunt, Hold or Guard - and they act after you, every turn. Army slots are limited, so choose what you bring. RELICS AND TRAITS Nineteen relics, each with levels that stack across a run. Seventeen lasting traits bought in the town between waves: extra turns before a wave lands, fewer enemies per wave, a free summon every wave, bank interest, a doubled army cap. No two runs build the same. BOSSES Ten bosses with real HP bars, from the Ogre Warchief to the Lich King, the Stone Titan and the Brood Queen. Act IV stops sending one king and starts sending a court - the final board holds three at once. THE TOWN Between waves, spend gold. Buy traits, promote your King into a Warlord, hire a new champion, or put gold in the bank and let it earn interest. FOUR HEROES Necromancer, Death Knight, Priestess, Ranger. Each moves differently, starts differently, and each has a relic only they can find. TAP ANYTHING Tap any piece to see its name, movement, attack and health. Gold squares preview where it steps, red squares preview what it can take. Learn the board before you commit. - Plays entirely offline, no required account - No ads, no timers, no energy system - Optional Game Center leaderboards and achievements - No in-app purchases; everything is earned in-run - Game controller support - iPhone and iPad - Pixel art and haptics If you can play chess, you can start. Whether you finish is another question.

en.title: RealTime Ai Cam
en.summary: RealTime AI Cam tells you what your camera is pointed at, out loud. Every part of it runs on the phone, so it works in airplane mode, on a subway, or in another country with no data. No account, no subscription, nothing to buy. WHAT IT DOES Names what is in front of you, over 600 everyday objects. What's this? describes the whole scene in a sentence and reads it to you. Hold to ask a question about what it sees, and it answers first: yes, no, or the number. Reads printed text out loud, and says numbers and dates the way a person would. Help Me Aim: say what you are looking for, a face, a page, a label, and it talks you into the shot, then takes the picture itself once you are lined up. One tap flashlight for dark rooms. Translates printed text into English. Distance to what is in front of you on iPhones with a depth sensor. LANGUAGES Built for English speakers. It reads English, and translates printed Spanish into English with no internet at all. Other languages download once from Apple, then work offline too (iOS 18 and later). WHAT STAYS ON YOUR PHONE Everything runs on your phone. The only time the app goes online is to download a language pack, once, and only if you want to translate something besides English or Spanish. English and Spanish never touch the internet. WORKS WITH VOICEOVER Every button is labeled, so you can run the whole app without seeing the screen. You can also let VoiceOver do the talking instead of the app if you prefer. HONEST ABOUT WHAT IT IS The models are small enough to live on your phone, which is why it works with no signal, and it does get things wrong sometimes. It tells you when it is unsure rather than guessing confidently. BUILT FROM WHAT USERS ASK FOR Most of what is in here came from blind and low vision users emailing me and me building it that night. If something does not work with VoiceOver, or you want it to do something it does not do yet, email matt@ineedhemp.com .
en.body:
RealTime AI Camera provides instant object detection, English OCR, and Spanish-to-English translation - all offline. Point your camera to identify 600+ objects, read text aloud, or translate Spanish text to English. Features LiDAR distance measurement on supported devices. Perfect for accessibility, language learning, and everyday assistance. Works 100% offline with no data collection.

WORKS WITH VOICEOVER Every button is labeled, so you can run the whole app without seeing the screen. It reads printed text out loud, names what the camera is pointed at, and tells you how far away things are on phones with a depth sensor.

en.title: Pegfall: Bounce Roguelite
en.summary: Pegfall is a one-handed pegboard physics roguelite where every shot draws an orb from your deck. Aim, bounce through a living board, build ruthless combos, and descend into the Maw. PLAY WITH VOICEOVER ON iPHONE Accessible play turns on by itself while VoiceOver is running. The board is built around one Aim control, with Status, Board summary and Last result next to it. By default, swipe up or down on Aim to move through five named directions, from Far left to Far right, and hear the likely first hit. After that, physics decides, and the game tells you when bumpers or bouncing walls can change the path. Double-tap to fire. When the balls stop, you hear the damage and what is left on the board. Board scan reads the board from top to bottom. While aiming, Magic Tap starts it and a second Magic Tap stops it. Optional aim sounds and the Aim practice lesson, whose practice shot costs nothing, help you learn. While Accessible play is on and VoiceOver is running, an interstitial ad can appear at most once every three minutes, and only after a button you press. You hear a warning first and "Ad closed" after it, and the game waits until then. VoiceOver play has been tested on iPhone. If something is hard to reach, please tell us. ▸ READ THE BOARD, THEN SHOOT A dotted line previews the start of your shot, up to the first two pegs it hits. After that, physics takes over, so the planning happens before you fire. ▸ A CAMPAIGN THAT ENDS — 10 CHAPTERS, 200 FLOORS Every chapter is its own biome and ends on its own boss, and deeper chapters add new board rules. Each chapter resets your build; only the last relic you took carries over as an heirloom. Leave mid-run and continue from the start of that floor. ▸ BUILDS THAT STACK 20 orbs, 23 relics, 40 cards and three characters send each run in a different direction. Take a curse when the floor asks for one. ▸ THE BOARD FIGHTS BACK From the sixth floor of every chapter, the pegs you spend erode. From chapter 3, pairs of pegs are wired into circuits whose discharge goes straight through armour, and some bosses bring hazard or void pegs onto the board. ▸ ENDLESS, DAILY AND WEEKLY Dive without a floor beneath you, take the same daily board as everyone else, or race one shared weekly board with a single attempt. After a Daily, Weekly or Endless run, join the optional online leaderboard with a nickname. No sign-up. ▸ GET STRONGER AS YOU PLAY Spend essence in the Workshop on permanent upgrades to starting health, damage and block, and on themes, ball skins, faces, ball hats and sound packs. Unlock Dark Depths tiers. ▸ BADGES AND BALLS YOU CANNOT BUY Your achievements are badges on your Profile, with badges for finishing the Weekly Race week after week, playing the Daily Challenge on many days and going deep in Endless. Three of them unlock a ball that is not for sale: Racer, Summit and Abyssal can only be unlocked by playing. ▸ THEMES AND SOUNDS IN THE SHOP The Iznik, Bosphorus and Sakura themes (try each first), the Music Box sound theme and melody packs your pegs play (listen first). ▸ MADE TO BE PLAYED BY MORE PEOPLE VoiceOver play on iPhone, VoiceOver labels and spoken purchase confirmations throughout the Workshop and the Shop, clear combat feedback, special pegs marked by more than colour, Reduce Motion support and 44 pt touch targets. Special thanks to accessibility tester Matheus Rheine, who helped shape VoiceOver play. ▸ MOBILE-NATIVE True portrait, one-handed, free to start. No energy timer and no premium wall. Monetization: optional rewarded continues, a Remove Ads purchase that stops interstitial ads, themes, looks and sound packs, and essence pouches. Essence also comes from playing.

Peg types use shapes as well as colour, so every board reads clearly. ▸ FAIR — SKILL, NOT LUCK A dotted trajectory preview shows where your shot lands. Every bounce is yours. ▸ A CAMPAIGN THAT ENDS — 10 CHAPTERS, 200 FLOORS Face ten bosses across distinct boards, palettes and rules. en.title: Accessimind Screen Reader
en.summary: Accessimind Reader is a screen reader application developed to enable visually impaired and partially sighted users to use their Android phones more clearly, quickly, and…
en.body:
Published 19 September 2026 by Sarper Arıkan

Accessimind Reader is a screen reader application developed to enable visually impaired and partially sighted users to use their Android phones more clearly, quickly, and independently.

Accessimind Reader uses the Android AccessibilityService API to provide screen reading functions. AccessibilityService is used to provide audio versions of on-screen content, detect user interface elements, navigate with gestures, provide audio feedback on focused items, and deliver a screen reader experience. This service is necessary for the screen reading feature, which is the core function of the application, to work.

Accessimind Reader does not use AccessibilityService for user tracking, displaying advertisements, remotely recording calls, bypassing Android security mechanisms, or modifying user settings without permission.

The application presents audio feedback, gesture navigation, keyboard shortcuts, clipboard operations, reading preferences, and tools for the focused item in a practical accessibility flow. The context menu provides quick access to frequently used areas such as reading controls, clipboard operations, notification access, focused item operations, and Accessimind settings.

Key Features:

Accessimind Reader is designed for users who need voice output and fast navigation. It focuses on providing predictable controls, understandable labels, and quick access to frequently used screen reader operations.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

Accessimind is a screen reader. Users can test it to see how well its features work for them and fit their needs.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

Android 16

en.title: iPhone 18 Pro: Hands-On and Initial Impressions
en.summary: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will be available to customers on Friday, September 18, 2026. Ahead of the launch, Apple sent me an iPhone 18 Pro for review. While a full review will come once I’ve had the opportunity to live with iPhone 18 Pro for a while, I do have some initial impressions that I wanted to share. First, and perhaps most noticeably, iPhone 18 Pro has what I would describe as a really big sound for its size. When compared side-by-side to iPhone 17 Pro Max—a device much larger and, presumably, with a bigger bottom speaker—iPhone 18 Pro sounds warmer, fuller, and lacks the treble over-emphasis I observed on the iPhone 17 Pro Max. If I had to describe the sound of iPhone 18 Pro, it would be ‘more complete’. And I do not think it is just software-side equalization: even at a relatively low 25% volume, iPhone 18 Pro has more bass and overall ‘presence’. My best guess is that Apple has made some hardware changes to the speaker on iPhone 18 Pro, and hopefully the iPhone 18 Pro Max too. One last note on sound for now: the earpiece speaker sounds warmer and fuller, as well. Beyond the speaker, iPhone 18 Pro contains some useful under-the-hood improvements, one of which I was not expecting to notice. Compared to last year’s models, iPhone 18 Pro has a larger vaper chamber inside the device for added cooling capacity. This is not just something you hear about at a Keynote and that's the end of it: picking up iPhone 18 Pro on multiple occasions, I noticed how literally 'cool' it felt to the touch. And even after multiple long phone calls on two different occasions, iPhone 18 Pro did not feel warm the way my iPhone 17 Pro Max does under similar circumstances. Cellular performance on iPhone 18 Pro's Apple-designed C2 Modem seems very good so far. On T-Mobile in Chicago, I got speeds right around a gigabyte down while indoors and a grand total of 1,109 Mbps down / 236 Mbps up when outdoors. This is not unheard-of for my area, but it is also not the norm, either. I will continue to test this throughout the review period. In terms of performance from the A20 Pro processor, VoiceOver (the built-in screen reader for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision people) is as fast and responsive as one could possibly want it to be. The moment I put my finger on the screen, VoiceOver is off and talking. That said, VoiceOver in iOS 27 already runs exceptionally well on the A19 series of chips from last year’s devices, and there’s only so much “can this be any more responsive?” before you hit an inevitable ceiling. Is VoiceOver ‘more’ responsive on the A20 Pro processor in iPhone 18 Pro than last year’s A19 Pro? Yes, but not by much—and again, this is only because VoiceOver already runs so well on last year’s A19-equipped devices to begin with. And that’s about all I can confidently speak to right now. Battery life seems good so far, though of course it’s day one and any serious testing will need to wait until after the various background tasks finish in the next couple days. Performance is good. Sound is very good. Call quality and cellular performance also seem good. I am excited for the coming weeks. Watch this space.

en.title: Learn How to Work More Effectively with PDFs and JAWS
en.summary: PDF documents are everywhere, from reports and forms to manuals and online resources. These documents can be accessed via a web browser or application like Adobe Acrobat Reader. When PDFs are formatted correctly, they can be read using standard navigation commands and JAWS Quick Navigation Keys; however, challenges arise when the PDF is not structured …
en.body:
PDF documents are everywhere, from reports and forms to manuals and online resources. These documents can be accessed via a web browser or application like Adobe Acrobat Reader.

When PDFs are formatted correctly, they can be read using standard navigation commands and JAWS Quick Navigation Keys; however, challenges arise when the PDF is not structured correctly. Details like headings, reading order, table structure, and labeled form fields — tell JAWS what to say and in what order. Whether that structure exists at all, and whether it matches what a sighted reader sees, is what separates an accessible PDF from an inaccessible one.

Join us Thursday, September 17 at noon ET for a live webinar, “Beyond the Basics: Working More Effectively with PDF Documents and JAWS.” We’ll delve deeper into these challenges and provide tips for navigating PDFs more efficiently.

In this webinar, we’ll provide an overview of PDFs, plus show you how to:

Register for this webinar to improve proficiency and productivity when working with PDFs, and learn some troubleshooting tips along the way. ACVREP credits will be available for those who attend the live webinar.

Can’t attend? We archive all webinars on our Webinars on Demand page. Have questions? Send an email to training@vispero.com .

en.title: Jieshuo Touch Focus And Double Tap Delays
en.summary: Whether you are exploring the screen or trying to find a specific element, there is a delay between touching the screen and focusing on the…
en.body:
Published 16 September 2026 by Kareen Kiwan

Whether you are exploring the screen or trying to find a specific element, there is a delay between touching the screen and focusing on the element under your finger. Similar to TalkBack, Jieshuo screen reader allows you to change the value of this delay. It also allows you to set the time in which 2 taps are registered as an accessibility double tap.

In order to change the touch focus delay and double tap delay values, you must first enable handling gestures directly through Jieshuo. To do this, go to Advanced settings > Operation settings and check the Handle gestures in the screen reader checkbox.

The next item in this section is for setting the touch focus delay value. Available values are 150, 200, 250, and 300 milliseconds. To change the time for double tap registration, select Double tap delay and choose any of the available values. The same values as those available for the touch focus delay are provided here.

In the same settings section, you will find an option called One-finger system gesture trigger range, with the following ranges: small, medium, big, and maximum. This setting defines the distance the finger needs to cover when performing one-finger system navigation gestures, such as swiping up from the bottom to go to Home.

Published in Tutorials

en.title: Apple Releases tvOS 27
en.summary: Apple has today released tvOS 27 for Apple TV 4K (2nd generation and later). According to Apple , tvOS 27 includes support for larger accessibility text sizes, high-resolution lossless audio in Apple Music, and a redesigned Podcasts app. More details should become available in the near future when Apple updates its "About Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD software updates" Apple Support document. Unfortunately, we were not able to test tvOS 27 during the beta cycle; and thus we do not have any information on whether this release contains any changes to vision accessibility features beyond the added support for larger text sizes. If you have upgraded to tvOS 27, we would greatly appreciate hearing your experiences with the update. To install tvOS 27, go to the Settings channel, then look for the System section near the bottom. From here, look for Software Updates under Maintenance, then select Update Software and Download and Install. Wait for your Apple TV to download the update. Don't disconnect or unplug your Apple TV until the update completes.

en.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 and iPadOS 27
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are now available to the public. (Note: As spotted by AppleVis Community Member TJT 2001 , Apple has also released iOS/iPadOS 26.7 for those not wishing to upgrade to iOS 27.) This post contains Apple's Release Notes for iOS 27, as well as links to all of AppleVis' content related to these updates. Also included are instructions on how to install the update. iOS 27 Release Notes iOS 27 introduces the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, as well as new features to help parents create safe digital experiences for kids, and improvements that make iOS more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. The next generation of Apple Intelligence also powers new features across apps that simplify the things you do every day, like editing images in Photos, communicating in Messages and Mail, and browsing in Safari. New parental controls and significant updates to Screen Time make it more intuitive and easy to use, so parents can feel confident that they're building the right digital experience for their child. And with improvements that span design, performance, connectivity, search, and more, the experience on iOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Siri mode in Camera integrates Visual Intelligence into the Camera app, letting you ask questions and take action with what's in front of you, like splitting a bill or looking up nutritional info for a plate of food. Write with Siri enables you to generate a draft from scratch, edit what you've written, or get feedback from Siri virtually anywhere you type. In Messages & Mail, Siri personalizes your writing style based on your relationships, and uses unique phrases and punctuation that you've previously used in your conversations with those people. Apple Intelligence across apps (All iPhone 16 models and later, iPhone 15 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro Max) Photos. Spatial Reframing lets you adjust the composition of a photo after it was taken by virtually changing the camera position. Extend tool intelligently expands images beyond their edges with realistic infill, so you can straighten horizons, change aspect ratios, or add more space around a subject. Clean Up supports removing even larger objects, with more realistic, high-quality results, and you can choose between Fast mode for small blemishes or High Quality for more intricate edits. Safari. Organize by Topic uses Apple Intelligence to sort your tabs, analyzing webpages and automatically grouping similar tabs together. Notify Me can periodically check a webpage for updates, like price changes and item availability. Describe an Extension lets you create a custom extension using natural language to adjust your view of a website's content or formatting. All-new Image Playground uses a new generative model to make high-quality images in virtually any style, including photorealistic, lets you modify your images using touch and natural language, and lets you generate Lock Screen wallpapers and Contact Posters with personalized suggestions. Describe a Shortcut lets you use natural language to create a shortcut or refine an existing one. Home. Summarized activity notifications combine related alerts across accessories into a single notification. Video descriptions for HomeKit Secure Video recordings summarize what's happening in a clip for eligible iCloud+ subscribers. Camera clip search lets you find specific moments from your HomeKit Secure Video cameras by searching in the Home app or Spotlight when on an eligible iCloud+ plan. Describe an event in Calendar lets you use natural language to create an event, and details like the time, location, invitees, and event title are filled in using Apple Intelligence. Suggestions in Mail help you take action based on the context of your emails, like getting directions to a restaurant you booked. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you're speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Accessibility. VoiceOver enhancements include more detailed and contextual image understanding for photos, charts, and screenshots, a conversational experience that lets you ask questions about your screen or surroundings, and a new way to get answers fast with an Action button integration. An enhanced Magnifier experience offers conversational visual assistance for users with low vision, with a high-contrast interface and natural language app controls for zooming and other Magnifier functions. A smarter Accessibility Reader uses intelligence to provide better text cleanup and formatting, images and tables, on-demand summaries, and translation. Voice Control flexible inputs help you navigate your device with just your voice by describing elements on screen in your own words, like "tap the gear" or "tap the button in the top right". And more, including additional ways to create and modify Genmoji, automatic proofreading, and more accurate dictation using an on-device model on iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Child Safety Improved setup experience for new child accounts lets parents choose the exact apps their kids can access when they set up an iPhone for their child. Ask to Browse gives parents the option to approve each new website before their child can view it. Expanded Communication Safety protections help intervene before children see gore or violent content in shared images and videos. Time Allowances help parents set boundaries around how long kids can use apps across Entertainment, Games, and Social Media apps, offering guidance based on expert research and tailored to each child's age. Schedules let parents choose which apps their kids can access at different points in their day and across weekdays and weekends. Redesigned Screen Time settings give parents at-a-glance information about how their kids use their devices, and controls to adjust access in just a few taps. System Improvements Liquid Glass refinements improve overall readability, and a new slider in Settings lets you personalize its appearance from ultra-clear to fully tinted . Faster performance in experiences across the system, including app launches, new photos loading in your Photos library, and AirDrop transfers. Improved search provides more relevant and comprehensive results in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Connectivity Assist enables more seamless transitions between Wi-Fi and cellular networks. And more improvements across apps and experiences, including enhancements to iCloud Shared Albums in Photos, Custom EQ for AirPods, support for perimenopause and menopause in Cycle Tracking in the Health app, and independent volume settings for Alarms and Timers. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Some features may not be available in all regions or on all iPhone models. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/ios/feature-availability/ Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 AppleVis iOS 27 Content AppleVis has the following content available for iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Blog Post: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements Blog Post: What's new in Accessibility in iOS 27 for Blind and DeafBlind Users , by Scott Davert Podcast: An Overview of the New VoiceOver and Braille Features in iOS 27 , by Michael Hansen Podcast: A Demonstration of the New Image Description Features in iOS 27 , by David Nason Podcast: A Demonstration and Walk-Through of the New Live Recognition Features in iOS 27 , by Levi Gobin How to Update iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 are available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update), via Finder on a Mac with macOS Catalina or later, or via iTunes on a PC or Mac with macOS Mojave or earlier. Before updating, we strongly recommend making a full and complete backup of your device (either locally or in iCloud, depending on personal preference). This will ensure that, in the unlikely event that something goes wrong during the update process, you will have a current backup on hand in case a device restore becomes necessary. Also, if using OTA update, we recommend plugging your device into a power source for the duration of the download/installation process, so as to prevent the unlikely event of your battery going dead during the update.

en.title: macOS Golden Gate: New Features, Changes, Improvements, and Bugs for Blind and Low Vision Users
en.summary: Apple has today released macOS 27 Golden Gate to the public. As usual, we won’t cover the mainstream features here, concentrating instead on what's new and changed for blind, DeafBlind, and low vision users. For an overview of the mainstream changes, we recommend this in-depth review by MacStories . Please remember to check the section about bugs to see if now is the right time to upgrade. There’s no harm in holding off a few weeks or months to let Apple address a problem you may find too disruptive to deal with. A note to braille users: the AppleVis team members doing testing with macOS Golden Gate are not heavy braille users. We have no information as to how well braille works in this release, so please keep this in mind when upgrading. If you are a braille user who has experience with Golden Gate, please share your findings in the comments to help the community. Changes for VoiceOver and Braille Users Improved Image and Screen Descriptions As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, VoiceOver in macOS Golden Gate can use Apple Intelligence to describe and answer questions about images or the current screen as it appears visually. Focusing on an image and pressing VO-Shift-L will describe the image, and you can find additional options, such as the ability to ask about an image, explore the image spatially, or describe the current screen, by pressing VO-Shift-R from anywhere in macOS. For added convenience, commands in this menu can be mapped in VoiceOver Utility > Commands. Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can. New Verbosity Options for Coding With macOS Golden Gate, you can customize how information such as line numbers, errors, and warnings are reported by VoiceOver in code editors like Xcode. These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings. New "Actions" rotor for trackpad users With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it. "Ducking Amount" setting The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound. Braille Improvements While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, text field labels can now be shown in braille. You can change the format these labels are presented in, or hide them entirely, by going to VoiceOver Utility > Braille > Layout, and clicking Text Field Labels. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, Braille Access in macOS Golden Gate supports plain text (txt) and portable document format (PDF) files. Improvements for Low Vision Users While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvement for low vision users: As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, content in Accessibility Reader can now be summarized and translated while retaining its original formatting on macOS Golden Gate. If you are a low vision Mac user, we would love to hear in the comments your experience and thoughts on this and any additional enhancements you encounter in macOS Golden Gate. Other Changes As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, the Aaron (English US), Arthur (English UK), Catherine (English Australia), Gordon (English Australia), and Martha (English UK) voices have been reintroduced with macOS Golden Gate. Like other voices, they can be used with Siri, as well as for accessibility functions like VoiceOver and Read & Speak. As on iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, subtitles for spoken dialog in videos where captioning is not already provided can be generated automatically in macOS Golden Gate. These can be turned on and adjusted when playing a video by clicking the "show legible media selection menu" button in the playback controls group. Writing Tools, previously accessed from many apps' Edit menus, as well as many text fields' context menus, is now accessed with VoiceOver by focusing on a text field and choosing "Show Writing Tools" from the Actions Menu. When toggling Cursor Tracking with VO-F3, its state is reflected in the "Mouse pointer:" popup menu in VoiceOver Utility. In prior versions of macOS, the state of Cursor Tracking was not reflected in this popup menu, which had the potential to confuse users. Change List In its support documentation, Apple lists the following changes for VoiceOver users in macOS Golden Gate: You can now turn off announcements that webpages send automatically, such as live scores, new messages, or status updates. Turn off Enable Web Announcements to silence announcements from a single area of a webpage or from the entire page. VoiceOver remembers your choice for that website, so the area stays silent the next time you visit. With the new Coding tab in the Verbosity category of VoiceOver Utility, you can choose whether VoiceOver announces line numbers, and whether it plays a tone or speaks a description when it encounters an error, a breakpoint, or the program counter. Bug Fixes and New Bugs for VoiceOver Users Below are lists of the bugs we believe to have been resolved in macOS Golden Gate, as well as new bugs introduced in this release. We strongly recommend that you read through the list of new bugs and any replies before updating, as this will allow you to make an informed decision on whether to install macOS Golden Gate or wait for a future release. While we are confident in the status of issues contained in this post, we do not claim that our bug list is definitive or that our assessments are infallible. Some issues may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features, and the number of available configurations and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and it is also likely that you will encounter issues that we did not experience during our own testing and daily use of macOS Golden Gate. To ensure the information here is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed macOS Golden Gate. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it's even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they're already aware of the ones listed here. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. Accessibility Bugs Resolved in macOS Golden Gate To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or Braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to macOS Golden Gate. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in macOS Tahoe have been resolved or meaningfully improved in macOS Golden Gate: VoiceOver no longer speaks list items on webpages unreliably. Pauses between sentences are no longer extended when using VoiceOver's "Say All" command. It is once again possible to reply to a message in the Message app by selecting the "Reply" action in the Actions menu. The Actions menu for Messages in the Messages app no longer contains redundant tapback actions. New Bugs for VoiceOver Users in macOS Golden Gate Our testing suggests that the following bugs have been introduced in macOS Golden Gate: After clicking the “Proofread” button in the Writing Tools popover using VoiceOver, only the Next, Previous, and Close buttons are visible, with no way to view the specific changes made to the text. There is no way to open or redownload apps from the “Apps & Purchases” page in the App Store using VoiceOver, with each app conveyed only as a button with no actions available and nothing to interact with besides the app’s name. To redownload a previously purchased app, you must click the [app name] button to open the product page, and then click the "Redownload" button in the toolbar. The sections and buttons in Safari’s Page Menu lack accessibility labels. Interacting with a section and pressing VO-Space on an item (all of which are clearly labeled) works to activate the item; however, interacting with each item in a section reveals an unlabeled button. When playing audio or video, VoiceOver announces “system has new window” once the media has started playing. The identity and purpose of this window is not clear from this announcement, and no new items appear in the application or window chooser menus. Revisit and resume past conversations in the new dedicated Siri app, synced with iCloud across your Apple devices. Siri AI is rolling out to users, and you can get started by turning it on in Settings. Take action on what’s onscreen With Visual Intelligence, you can select a window of your screen and Siri can answer questions or take action with what’s onscreen, like adding events to your calendar. You can access Visual Intelligence with a dedicated keyboard shortcut — Command-Shift-Space. Powerful new ways to edit photos Use intelligent photo editing tools to reframe a photo after it’s been taken with Spatial Reframing or expand your shot with the Extend tool. And enhancements to Clean Up let you remove distractions with better quality and more realistic infill, even when the scene is complex. New tools to browse in Safari Automatically group your tabs into topics, so related pages are easier to find. With Notify Me, Safari can monitor pages for changes like price drops or restocks and alert you when it’s time to act. Describe an Extension lets you use natural language to create custom extensions, like adding a button to save your favorite recipes. In Conclusion We would like to thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. We'd love to hear your thoughts after you've had a chance to install the upgrade. What new features do you find most useful? Are there any changes you don't like? Please share your feedback in the comments below. When doing so, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in macOS Golden Gate. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we thank Apple's Accessibility team for their prompt response in fixing many of the bugs reported during the macOS Golden Gate beta cycle. We encourage Apple to promptly address this and other outstanding accessibility issues discussed in this post and the comments below so that macOS can be as accessible, usable, and enjoyable as possible for all users. To install macOS Golden Gate, choose System Settings from the Apple menu, select General in the table, click Software Update in the scroll area, and click the Upgrade Now button to begin the upgrade process. If other updates are available, you can click the Info button to see details about them and select specific updates to install. More information on how to update the software on your Mac is available on this Apple Support page.

Note that while VoiceOver can describe and answer questions about what's on the screen, it cannot directly interact with elements like VOCR or Screen Recognition on iOS and iPadOS can.

These settings can be found in the new "Coding" tab in VoiceOver Utility > Verbosity. We do not currently know which code editors besides Xcode respect these settings.

With macOS Golden Gate, you can perform custom actions for the focused element, the same actions available in VoiceOver's Actions menu, using trackpad commands. To do this, enable trackpad commands if they're not already enabled, turn the rotor to "Actions," swipe up or down with one finger to select a custom action, and double-tap to activate it.

The "Ducking Amount" setting for determining how much other audio is ducked when VoiceOver is speaking, originally introduced with iOS 18 and iPadOS 18, has been brought to macOS with the release of Golden Gate. It can be found in VoiceOver Utility > Sound.

While it is not something we have been able to test, we are aware of the following improvements for braille users in macOS Golden Gate:

For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post.

en.title: watchOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver Features, Issues, and Improvements
en.summary: Apple has today released watchOS 27 to the public. watchOS 27 is compatible with the Apple Watch Series 9 and later and the Apple Watch Ultra 2 and later. Due to the inherent challenges of beta software testing on watchOS, our testing of watchOS 27 has been quite limited. That said, for VoiceOver users, there is at least one new bug that we are aware of and a handful of new features and improvements. New VoiceOver Bugs in watchOS 27 There is rather significant latency with VoiceOver speech when swiping through the user interface. Specifically, there is a delay between when the VoiceOver sound effects/haptics play, and when VoiceOver speaks. Our testing suggests that this issue is not synthesizer-specific. It is unclear to us whether this behavior is simply a function of the newer operating system encountering the limits of hardware (something that has historically been a challenge on Apple Watch devices), or whether this is something that can be resolved by Apple in a future software update. A Feedback report has been filed, and we will keep the community advised as additional information becomes available. If you identify any additional vision accessibility bugs in watchOS 27, please let us know by posting a comment. New VoiceOver Features and Improvements in watchOS 27 There is a new "Tap to Wake" toggle in VoiceOver settings. By default, the setting is enabled, and the Watch will be woken when you tap on the screen. Our best understanding is that disabling this feature should prevent the device from waking when the screen is tapped. It is now possible to customize the speaking of VoiceOver hints in watchOS. Available options are 'Always', 'Never', and 'App-Specific Hints'. On the Clock Face, VoiceOver now speaks the names of Complications before speaking their content. For example, VoiceOver might say, "Weather, Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees," instead of just saying "Mostly Sunny 65 Degrees." For braille display users, there is a new setting, "Translate After a Delay." There are other braille settings that we also believe may be new in this release, but our braille-related testing in watchOS is very limited and so this is not something we are able to comment on with any level of certainty. If you spot any other new features/changes in watchOS 27 or have any corrections to the above, please do let us know by posting a comment. watchOS 27 Release Notes watchOS 27 features the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, updates to Workout Buddy, a new tap gesture, a dynamic app grid to make it easier to access your most used apps, and improvements that make watchOS 27 more responsive and delightful to use. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri that is more intelligent, knowledgeable, and capable. With improvements that span areas like fitness, design, performance, and more, the experience on watchOS 27 has been refined and elevated, so it feels even better to use. Siri AI A more capable and conversational version of Siri is rolling out to users. It helps you find what you need and get more done, drawing on capabilities like personal context understanding, app actions, onscreen awareness, and access to broad world knowledge. New voice experience offers more expressive and natural-sounding voices, and lets you customize expressivity and pace to make Siri more personal to you using powerful on-device models on paired iPhone Air and iPhone 17 Pro models and later. Dedicated Siri app provides an easy way to revisit an existing conversation or kick off a new one, and privately syncs conversations across your Apple products with iCloud. Apple Intelligence across apps Workout Buddy delivers motivation with new insights and is now available without your iPhone nearby when you have a Wi-Fi or cellular connection. Call Context in the Phone app understands when you’re speaking to certain businesses and proactively surfaces relevant information from across your apps, like a confirmation code or a reservation number. Cycle Tracking Cycle deviation notifications that are suggestive of perimenopause can be received by those age 40 and over. Watch Faces Siri Modular face features a rectangular complication that mirrors the top widget of the Smart Stack, which dynamically updates to show the most relevant widget, as well as a Siri complication to quickly invoke Siri. Smart Stack Single-handed tap gesture enables you to tap your index finger and thumb together once to select a widget in the Smart Stack, even if your other hand is occupied. New suggestion widgets will be surfaced when most relevant to you, including a Parked Car location, birthday reminders for a close contact, balance changes on a transit card, Noise app after a loud noise notification, and more. System Improvements Dynamic app grid highlights your most popular and recently used apps. Find My app is now consolidated into one app to show People, Devices, and Items with a map-centric interface. Media playback now starts faster. Workout app makes distance calculations during treadmill workouts even more accurate from the first step of every walk or run. Fitness app features more accurate route maps after workouts. Battery extension notifications may be proactively offered to disable certain features to increase battery life, including gestures, Start Workout reminders, and Raise to Speak method of invoking Siri. Shazam in the Smart Stack and Music Recognition app identifies songs offline without an internet connection and delivers results automatically when you’re back online. Liquid Glass refinements improve readability with more uniform refraction and improved contrast. For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit: https://support.apple.com/100100 Usage limits may apply for some Apple Intelligence features. To learn more, please visit: https://www.apple.com/apple-intelligence Software updates, like this one, add new features and improvements that may affect performance and/or battery life. To learn more, please visit: https://support.apple.com/125039 How to Update watchOS 27 is available via Over-the-Air Update (Settings > General > Software Update) or by going to the Watch app on your iPhone and navigating to General > Software Update. To install the update, your Watch must be connected to its charger and have at least 50% battery power.
