en.title: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Summary of VoiceOver and Braille Issues and Improvements
en.summary: iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 were released to the public on Monday, September 14, 2026. This post contains a summary of new bugs and fixes impacting VoiceOver and Braille support that the AppleVis Editorial Team has independently validated during our use and testing of these releases. The information contained in this post is compiled from our own use and testing of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 during the beta period from June to September 2026; as well as from validated reports submitted by others through our Community Bug Program and shared on the AppleVis Forum. Our sincere appreciation goes to everyone who so generously took the time to share their findings with us. At the outset, we need to state explicitly that the bug list contained in this post is not definitive and that our assessments are not infallible. While we are confident in the presence of the issues discussed in this post, there are many other reports shared on the AppleVis Forum by members of our community that we have not been able to independently replicate with the available information. Many of these reports represented use cases that are different from those of our team; and a small number were issues that, despite understanding how to reproduce them, we did not get the same results. We say all of this so that readers understand the limits of our own testing, and that others' experiences may be different from ours. An issue not being present in our bug list does not mean the issue does not exist; it simply means that we are either unaware of or unable to reproduce it. As is our routine practice, each bug in this post has been given a severity rating. These ratings are based upon what we believe to be the implications for accessing and using features and functionality for the average user; the level of impact on the overall user experience; and whether or not there is an effective workaround for the issue. However, as these ratings are subjective to an extent, it is very possible that they may not reflect your own opinion or use case. With this in mind, we strongly recommend reading this full post and any replies before updating to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27; as we believe this will help you make an informed decision on whether to install the software at the current time or to wait for a future release. We also strongly recommend that you read this Megathread about the iOS 27 RC , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software. Some issues listed in this post and on the Forum may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features and the number of devices, available configurations, and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and you likely will not agree with every severity rating for the bugs that you do experience. While we wish it were otherwise, this is to be expected. And as is the nature with all software, it is also likely that you will encounter issues that are not reported in this post. To ensure the information in this post is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it is even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they are already aware of the ones listed in this post. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post. With all of the preamble out of the way, below are the new bugs for VoiceOver and Braille users which members of the AppleVis Editorial Team have personally experienced and believe to be present in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: A Major Change to VoiceOver's Audio Profile In iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, there is a significant change in the sound profile of VoiceOver when the device's internal speaker is used. When compared to iOS 26, VoiceOver audio in iOS 27 has significantly less bass, particularly at lower volume levels. The resulting sound might best be described as 'neutral' or 'flat', with significantly less of the low-end emphasis and other processing that has characterized VoiceOver audio in recent versions of iOS/iPadOS. If you have not yet upgraded to iOS 27, we believe that you can get a reasonable approximation of how VoiceOver will sound on your device by making a phone call, putting the call on speaker, and then using VoiceOver to navigate around the screen; as the flatter, more neutral sound profile that VoiceOver uses during a phone call sounds very similar to what we are hearing in iOS 27. At the time of publication, we do not know whether the change to VoiceOver's sound profile is expected behavior; thus, we are not including it in our bug list. Nevertheless, we feel that users should be aware of this change before upgrading. If we receive additional information, we will update this post accordingly. Serious Bugs When the state of an item changes or the screen updates, VoiceOver does not always recognize/speak the information. This issue has many manifestations, including (but not limited to): When waking the device, VoiceOver may speak the time the device was last woken rather than the current time; When information updates onscreen (such as the status of an operation in an app), VoiceOver may not speak it right away and instead speak the previously displayed text. There is no known workaround, though VoiceOver will eventually speak the updated information if focus is moved off of and back onto the impacted element enough times. The VoiceOver Per-Voice Equalizer (a feature that allows one to customize certain frequency/tonal characteristics of a voice) does not work. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the per-voice Equalizer, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. The VoiceOver Pronunciation Dictionary does not work reliably, with custom pronunciations often not being obeyed by VoiceOver. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the Pronunciation Dictionary, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved. If an external audio device is connected, VoiceOver speech does not work when playing audio in Safari. Pausing the audio causes it to start working again. Sometimes, when reading text, VoiceOver stops speaking and does not resume on its own. This issue does not occur all of the time. When it does occur, speech will stop mid-sentence (and sometimes even mid-word). Touching the screen or performing a touch gesture (like a one-finger swipe left or right) restores speech, and the user can then refocus VoiceOver on the impacted element. In iOS 27's new Recovery Menu, there is no spoken feedback in Diagnostics Mode, rendering this option completely inaccessible. There is no known workaround to make Diagnostics Mode itself usable. If you do manage to accidentally get your device into Diagnostics Mode, our experience is that the device will restart into normal operation after approximately five to ten minutes of inactivity. Moderate Bugs On some devices, Sound Curtain and Touch Curtain do not work. For affected users, this issue can be worked around by: Manually enabling these settings by going to Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver > Braille > Sound Curtain, or Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver > Braille > Touch curtain respectively. For Sound Curtain, lowering the device volume to 0%. Adding the Sound Curtain to VoiceOver's Quick Settings to save a few steps. Head to Settings > Accessibility > VoiceOver > Quick Settings and select "Sound curtain." Since Touch Curtain does not have a Quick Settings option, this workaround does not apply. In Safari, the buttons to switch between the Start Page, Reading List, History, and Bookmarks do not work. It is possible to select these buttons, and VoiceOver indicates they have been selected, but the content itself does not update, meaning content cannot be reached. As a workaround, perform a one-finger triple-tap (what is known as a "long press") on the desired button to activate it. Our thanks to AppleVis user Brian Giles for this workaround. When VoiceOver focus is placed inside a text field, and then subsequently moved onto a combo box, the menu automatically opens. On occasions, when swiping through the Lock Screen using one-finger swipe right or left, VoiceOver focus may be inconsistent. When navigating through the Lock Screen using a one-finger swipe right, after the "Swipe up to Unlock" element, the expected behavior is that VoiceOver will focus on the first notification (if present); Focus status (if present); or the first item on the screen, like Flashlight or Camera. However, sometimes, VoiceOver users may find that focus is instead placed on items from the Status Bar, such as Cellular Carrier, Battery Percentage, or the Clock. If VoiceOver focus does land on items from the Status Bar when swiping, it is sometimes possible to continue swiping to the right and get to the first Lock Screen item; however, other times, VoiceOver focus can become stuck in a loop between the time, the "Swipe Up to Unlock" element, Cellular Carrier, an element with no spoken or audible feedback, or any combination of the above. Sometimes, VoiceOver does not speak the time when the device is woken with the Side Button. If this issue occurs, single-tap the screen with one finger to wake the device. After prompting Siri with the Side button, revealing the interface at the top of the screen, nothing happens when double-tapping the "Open in App" button. Double-tapping this button should work to activate it, opening the conversation in the Siri app. In the Phone App, the buttons to switch between 'All' and 'Missed' do not work. This issue can be worked around by either switching to Unified View or swiping through all calls in Classic View. Our thanks to AppleVis user Brian Giles for this workaround. Sometimes, it is not possible to access notifications with VoiceOver that are visually displayed onscreen. Typically, the 'Show notifications' button is present, but on these intermittent occasions, selecting it fails to reveal the notifications, and does nothing. If this issue occurs, double-tap and hold on the "Show Notifications" button, and swipe up. This will reveal the notifications. VoiceOver's 'Copy Speech' function copies the full semantic markup and hints, instead of just the spoken text. For example, in iOS 27, Copy Speech might paste "Latest news, heading Level 2". In previous versions of iOS, Copy Speech would only paste "Latest news," which is the desired behavior. Screen Recognition does not appear in VoiceOver's Quick Settings panel, even if selected for inclusion. The Camera App contains extraneous elements for editing Camera Controls when Edit Mode is not active. This includes "Remove" elements next to each camera control and a "Done" button that does nothing when tapped. When an app is open and VoiceOver focus is placed on the battery indicator, it is not possible to swipe to other items on the status bar. The Direct Touch option in the VoiceOver Quick Settings panel does not work. Minor Bugs In Notification Center, the Rotor Action for clearing all notifications does not work. As a workaround, Locate and double-tap on the "Clear, Notification Center" button, then double-tap on the "Confirm Clear, Notification Center" button that appears. Our thanks to AppleVis Community member Sieghard Weitzel for this workaround. On the Keypad in the Phone app, the button to place the call is labeled as "Call Answer." When focusing on a conversation in the Siri app, the Actions rotor for the conversation contains two identical "Delete" actions. When the device is set to 24-Hour Time, VoiceOver does not correctly speak the time on the top of the hour. When customising VoiceOver touch gestures and you select to replace the current command with a new one, the old command is sometimes not overwritten, necessitating manual removal and replacement. When the Safari toolbar is set to 'Bottom', the "Show Bookmarks" button is incorrectly labelled as "Bookmark." When the VoiceOver cursor reaches the first or last element onscreen in the Camera app, focus loops instead of stopping at the boundary. Improvements for VoiceOver and Braille in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in iOS/iPadOS 26 have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27: Stability of VoiceOver focus has been significantly improved across the operating system. The screen no longer locks while VoiceOver is reading a notification on the Lock Screen. Keyboard sounds once again play when VoiceOver is on, regardless of the audio ducking setting. VoiceOver focus is no longer erratic in the App Switcher when it is opened from the Home Screen. The default volume of the Eloquence speech synthesizer more closely matches that of other voices. In Conclusion Our team has compiled lists of new vision accessibility bugs for every major iOS and iPadOS release since iOS 7 in 2013. No software from any manufacturer is completely free of bugs. That said, the number of bugs - particularly those classified as "serious" and involving core VoiceOver and braille functionality - in iOS/iPadOS 27 is deeply concerning. We call on Apple to urgently prioritize fixing the bugs listed in this post, as well as those on The AppleVis Bug Tracker . If you have not already upgraded to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27, we would strongly recommend that you take a few moments to read through any replies to this post before doing so; in case other users' experiences differ from our own. Also, consider that historically, Apple has delivered fixes for many accessibility bugs within the first few x.x.1 updates following major releases, and waiting briefly may allow Apple to resolve any initial problems reported after the public release. In the event that you do encounter an issue that is particularly bothersome, there are some troubleshooting steps you can take. Sometimes, simply toggling VoiceOver off and on again or restarting your device can resolve some issues that may arise following an OS update. Therefore, we highly recommend including these steps as part of your standard troubleshooting process. If restarting VoiceOver and/or your device does not resolve the issue, it might be worth considering a reset of your VoiceOver Settings; to do this, navigate to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Reset VoiceOver Settings. While this approach requires manually reconfiguring your customized VoiceOver settings, we have heard of multiple instances where a VoiceOver settings reset resolved issues since this feature became available in last year's iOS 26. This suggests that occasionally, problems can be attributed to local factors rather than being OS bugs. Finally, when commenting below, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information. Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Comments criticizing others' decisions are not constructive and do nothing to add to the discussion; but they do set a negative tone and get in the way of readers finding helpful information. Furthermore, not experiencing an issue yourself does not mean that it doesn't exist for others, as bugs can be configuration-specific. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. Our aim with these posts is to provide a forum for respectful, constructive, and honest sharing of experiences that inform decisions and empower people. In closing, we would like to again thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the iOS/iPadOS 27 beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Our information about this release is more complete because of you, and we are very grateful to all who took the time to contribute. Updates to this post Following initial publication, this post has been updated to more accurately reflect our current knowledge of iOS 27/iPadOS 27 bugs and workarounds. Specific changes include: Downgraded Sound Curtain/Touch Curtain bug from serious to moderate, and expanded on known workarounds. Added attribution of a workaround to a bug in the Phone app to Brian Giles.
en.body:
iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 were released to the public on Monday, September 14, 2026. This post contains a summary of new bugs and fixes impacting VoiceOver and Braille support that the AppleVis Editorial Team has independently validated during our use and testing of these releases.

The information contained in this post is compiled from our own use and testing of iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 during the beta period from June to September 2026; as well as from validated reports submitted by others through our Community Bug Program and shared on the AppleVis Forum. Our sincere appreciation goes to everyone who so generously took the time to share their findings with us.

At the outset, we need to state explicitly that the bug list contained in this post is not definitive and that our assessments are not infallible. While we are confident in the presence of the issues discussed in this post, there are many other reports shared on the AppleVis Forum by members of our community that we have not been able to independently replicate with the available information. Many of these reports represented use cases that are different from those of our team; and a small number were issues that, despite understanding how to reproduce them, we did not get the same results. We say all of this so that readers understand the limits of our own testing, and that others' experiences may be different from ours. An issue not being present in our bug list does not mean the issue does not exist; it simply means that we are either unaware of or unable to reproduce it.

As is our routine practice, each bug in this post has been given a severity rating. These ratings are based upon what we believe to be the implications for accessing and using features and functionality for the average user; the level of impact on the overall user experience; and whether or not there is an effective workaround for the issue. However, as these ratings are subjective to an extent, it is very possible that they may not reflect your own opinion or use case. With this in mind, we strongly recommend reading this full post and any replies before updating to iOS 27 and iPadOS 27; as we believe this will help you make an informed decision on whether to install the software at the current time or to wait for a future release. We also strongly recommend that you read this Megathread about the iOS 27 RC , as it contains a wealth of community reports about and experiences with the Release Candidate version of the software.

Some issues listed in this post and on the Forum may manifest only under specific conditions; this is all the more likely as software continues to add more features and the number of devices, available configurations, and use cases in Apple's ecosystem continues to grow. You likely will not experience every bug that we list, and you likely will not agree with every severity rating for the bugs that you do experience. While we wish it were otherwise, this is to be expected. And as is the nature with all software, it is also likely that you will encounter issues that are not reported in this post.

To ensure the information in this post is as complete and accurate as possible, we would appreciate input from those who have installed iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. Please confirm if you are encountering the same problems listed or if you have found workarounds. Please also let us know about any additional issues not mentioned here. Of course, it is even more important that you report any new bugs directly to Apple - they are already aware of the ones listed in this post. For an explanation of why and how to report bugs to Apple, see this post.

With all of the preamble out of the way, below are the new bugs for VoiceOver and Braille users which members of the AppleVis Editorial Team have personally experienced and believe to be present in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27:

In iOS 27 and iPadOS 27, there is a significant change in the sound profile of VoiceOver when the device's internal speaker is used. When compared to iOS 26, VoiceOver audio in iOS 27 has significantly less bass, particularly at lower volume levels. The resulting sound might best be described as 'neutral' or 'flat', with significantly less of the low-end emphasis and other processing that has characterized VoiceOver audio in recent versions of iOS/iPadOS.

If you have not yet upgraded to iOS 27, we believe that you can get a reasonable approximation of how VoiceOver will sound on your device by making a phone call, putting the call on speaker, and then using VoiceOver to navigate around the screen; as the flatter, more neutral sound profile that VoiceOver uses during a phone call sounds very similar to what we are hearing in iOS 27.

At the time of publication, we do not know whether the change to VoiceOver's sound profile is expected behavior; thus, we are not including it in our bug list. Nevertheless, we feel that users should be aware of this change before upgrading. If we receive additional information, we will update this post accordingly.

When the state of an item changes or the screen updates, VoiceOver does not always recognize/speak the information. This issue has many manifestations, including (but not limited to):

There is no known workaround, though VoiceOver will eventually speak the updated information if focus is moved off of and back onto the impacted element enough times.

The VoiceOver Per-Voice Equalizer (a feature that allows one to customize certain frequency/tonal characteristics of a voice) does not work. There is no known workaround. If you rely on the per-voice Equalizer, we recommend that you do not install iOS/iPadOS 27 until this issue is resolved.

To the best of our knowledge, Apple does not routinely publish lists of bug fixes for VoiceOver or braille across releases; thus, it is difficult to get a complete accounting of every issue that has been resolved or what fixes users can expect to see upon upgrading to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27. With this in mind, our testing suggests that the following issues present in iOS/iPadOS 26 have been resolved or meaningfully improved in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27:

Our team has compiled lists of new vision accessibility bugs for every major iOS and iPadOS release since iOS 7 in 2013. No software from any manufacturer is completely free of bugs. That said, the number of bugs - particularly those classified as "serious" and involving core VoiceOver and braille functionality - in iOS/iPadOS 27 is deeply concerning. We call on Apple to urgently prioritize fixing the bugs listed in this post, as well as those on The AppleVis Bug Tracker .

If you have not already upgraded to iOS 27 or iPadOS 27, we would strongly recommend that you take a few moments to read through any replies to this post before doing so; in case other users' experiences differ from our own. Also, consider that historically, Apple has delivered fixes for many accessibility bugs within the first few x.x.1 updates following major releases, and waiting briefly may allow Apple to resolve any initial problems reported after the public release.

In the event that you do encounter an issue that is particularly bothersome, there are some troubleshooting steps you can take. Sometimes, simply toggling VoiceOver off and on again or restarting your device can resolve some issues that may arise following an OS update. Therefore, we highly recommend including these steps as part of your standard troubleshooting process.

If restarting VoiceOver and/or your device does not resolve the issue, it might be worth considering a reset of your VoiceOver Settings; to do this, navigate to Settings> Accessibility> VoiceOver> Reset VoiceOver Settings. While this approach requires manually reconfiguring your customized VoiceOver settings, we have heard of multiple instances where a VoiceOver settings reset resolved issues since this feature became available in last year's iOS 26. This suggests that occasionally, problems can be attributed to local factors rather than being OS bugs.

Finally, when commenting below, we ask that you please keep the discussion focused on accessibility issues specifically introduced or fixed in iOS 27 and iPadOS 27. Our release posts tend to be widely read and garner many helpful responses, so it is all the more important that readers can easily find relevant information.

Also, please remember that upgrade decisions are personal, with each user's situation unique - there is no right or wrong choice. Stating that an issue doesn't exist simply because you haven't encountered it is unhelpful. In closing, we would like to again thank everyone in our community who contributed to AppleVis' testing and bug-reporting efforts during the iOS/iPadOS 27 beta cycle - be it through our Community Bug Program or just by posting on our Forum. Published 14 September 2026 by Aleksandar Đurić

NetBoard turns your computer into an instant input device for your phone, allowing you to type quickly, accurately, and effortlessly using your computer’s full physical keyboard.

Built from the ground up with accessibility (A11y) as a core value, NetBoard is designed for blind, visually impaired, and motor-impaired users who find mobile touchscreen keyboards challenging to use with screen readers such as TalkBack.

Windows app: Download NetBoard for Windows .

NetBoard does not collect, log, or store your keystrokes, clipboard history, or audio files. Data is encrypted and processed strictly in transit. The app contains no ads and has no hidden fees.

The app is fully accessible because it was developed by a blind programmer.

es.title: Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3
es.summary: Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación, la beta 2 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3" La entrada Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 2 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 2 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es d26386e7ac3ac6d245c8adcfc82c07e9332278360af3396b69888b6b31e08d33. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la segunda beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.title: Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK)
en.summary: Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK) is an Android keyboard for blind and low-vision users. Refined over many years together with blind users, it was rebuilt from…
en.body:
Published 13 September 2026 by Philip Heyse

Blind Accessibility Keyboard (BAK) is an Android keyboard for blind and low-vision users. Refined over many years together with blind users, it was rebuilt from the ground up in summer 2026: modern, faster, and adjustable in great detail.

Two ways to type, both letting you check a key before it is sent:

– Lift to Type: slide your finger over the keys, hear each one, and commit by lifting it – Double Tap to Type: the first tap reads the key, a second tap confirms it

1. Setup and settings:

Setup is guided step by step and confirms out loud when the keyboard is enabled and selected.

The settings screen is made for TalkBack: a switch and its label are read as one element, and sections announced with a “Section:” prefix.

Settings can be saved to a file and restored later. A session log can be exported or e-mailed if you need help.

2. Keyboard layouts:

264 layouts are included. For most languages you can choose between Simple (four rows), Fluent Flow (five rows with numbers), Fluent Flow with Cursor (plus cursor keys), PC (Ctrl, Alt and function keys), PC with Num Pad, and Robo Gear (familiar from standard smartphone keyboards).

Hold the space bar for the Quick Menu to switch layouts. The full list of languages is at the end of this text.

The app itself is translated into 30 languages, including Finnish, Malay and Urdu.

3. What you hear:

– Adjustable speed and pitch, with upper and lower case told apart by pitch – Choice of speech engine, with language, country and voice – Optional NATO alphabet, so “B” and “D” are never confused – Spoken names for punctuation, symbols and emoji – Announcements when the keyboard opens or closes, when you move between letters, numbers, symbols and emoji, and on Shift, Alt or Ctrl changes – Key click sounds in three styles, with adjustable volume – Vibration when typing and on gestures, each switchable separately

4. Voice input:

Start dictation with the microphone key or the Quick Menu, and choose between:

– Your device’s own dictation – A model running on your device: no account needed, works offline, though less accurate than the online options – Popular AI services, using your own API key, stored encrypted on your device only

5. Typing support:

– Auto-correct for many of the supported languages. One Backspace restores the original word. Never runs in password fields. – Text shortcuts: “brt” becomes “Best regards, Tom”. One Backspace undoes it. – Clipboard history above the keys. Tap an entry to insert it. – Your own keys for text you often need, such as your e-mail address – Optional capital letter at the start of a sentence – Adjustable delay and repeat speed when holding Delete or Backspace

6. Subscription:

BAK is funded by a small subscription. It costs less than the equivalent of one US dollar per month, and follows the local price level, so in many countries it is lower. It pays for ongoing work: fixing bugs, keeping up with new Android versions, and adding features. Before subscribing, you can try the keyboard in the test field on the app’s home screen. A subscription is needed to use it in other apps.

7. Help and contact: – https://bright-side.de/bak/ – ba * @ ********* de.de

The Help section in the app has the documentation, the mailing list, and a way to e-mail the developer.

8. Layouts for your language:

Arabic (also with French), Belarusian, Bengali, Bulgarian (Cyrillic, Latin, Phonetic), Canadian (also French, Multilingual), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English (UK, USA), French (France, Switzerland), German (Germany, Switzerland), Greek, Gujarati, Hebrew, Hindi (also InScript), Hungarian, Indonesian, Italian (Italy, Switzerland), Kannada, Marathi, Norwegian, Persian, Polish (also programmer), Portuguese (also Brazilian ABNT), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Spanish (Spain, Latin America), Swedish, Tamil, Telugu, Turkish (F and Q), Ukrainian, Vietnamese.

Free or paid:

Accessibility and User Comments:

The keyboard app was specifically designed for blind or visually impaired users.

Last Tested App version and Android version:

5.0.7

es.title: Accesibilidad y Tecnología Vive el fútbol accesible con Movistar Touch en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.summary: Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.
es.body:
Gracias a la colaboración entre la ONCE, Movistar y el Atlético de Madrid, las personas afiliadas podrán disfrutar de una experiencia más accesible e inmersiva durante los partidos de fútbol que se celebren en el estadio Riyadh Air Metropolitano.

Se trata de Movistar Touch , un servicio gratuito dirigido a aficionados con entrada para el encuentro, que permite seguir el desarrollo del partido mediante audiodescripción y una tableta háptica capaz de reproducir en tiempo real la posición del balón sobre el terreno de juego. Esta tecnología ofrece una nueva forma de vivir la emoción del fútbol y constituye un excelente ejemplo de cómo la innovación puede contribuir a derribar barreras y favorecer la participación de todas las personas.

Actualmente, el Riyadh Air Metropolitano es el único estadio de España que ofrece este sistema. Las personas afiliadas interesadas en utilizarlo deberán solicitarlo previamente enviando un correo electrónico a inclusion@atleticodemadrid.com , indicando el partido de LALIGA para el que desean adquirir entradas y hacer uso del servicio.

Es importante tener en cuenta que Movistar Touch dispone de un número limitado de unidades, por lo que se recomienda realizar la solicitud con la mayor antelación posible.

Esta iniciativa se enmarca en la colaboración que el Atlético de Madrid mantiene desde hace años con la ONCE y Fundación ONCE para seguir mejorando la accesibilidad de sus instalaciones y servicios, reforzando así su compromiso con un deporte más inclusivo y accesible para todos.

en.title: Issue Affecting Some JAWS and Fusion Features Now Resolved
en.summary: The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features …
en.body:
The issue we reported on September 4 has been resolved with no action needed on your part.

Last week a Microsoft update changed the way accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS was not always receiving the information it needed from those applications, and some features provided no speech or braille. This affected the JAWS Results Viewer, OCR Viewer, Picture Smart, and Message Center, along with New Outlook and Microsoft Copilot 365.

On September 6 we deployed a temporary change to JAWS so that customers would not have to wait while the underlying problem was still being investigated. On September 7 Microsoft released an update that corrected the root cause. Because that update resolves the problem at its source, we have since removed our temporary change.

The Microsoft update is delivered automatically, so there is nothing for you to install or turn on. The temporary work-around we shared last week, toggling the Touch Cursor off and on, is no longer needed.

If you are still experiencing the problem, please restart your computer so the Microsoft update can take effect. If that does not resolve it, please contact your local dealer or our technical support team.

We appreciate everyone who reported this to us and who let us know when things began working again. Those reports helped us confirm the cause quickly and gave us what we needed to work with Microsoft toward a resolution.

en.title: In-Process 8th September 2026
en.summary: It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new: NVDA 2026.2 Magnifier A new Beta already? Resetting to Factory Defaults NVDA 2026.2 NVDA 2026.2 has been released! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.… Read More
en.body:
It’s a busy and exciting time – it’s release time! Let’s dive in and see what’s new:

NVDA 2026.2 has been released ! This release includes a new built-in Magnifier feature, improvements to touch gestures and navigation, and expanded speech and braille capabilities.

The Magnifier provides zoom and color filtering options to assist users with visual impairments. The Magnifier currently only supports full screen mode, with docked modes planned in a future release. Touch support has been significantly expanded with new pinch gestures and touch-based browse mode navigation for web content. You can now navigate between links, headings, form fields, and other elements using touch flicks.

Speech features have been enhanced with support for custom speech dictionaries that can be provided by add-ons and new dictionary entry types for more granular control. A new voice setting for OneCore voices was added to control pauses after punctuation. A new command allows repeating the last spoken information, with the ability to display it in a browsable message. The default gesture to repeat the last spoken information is NVDA+x , which can be changed in the Input Gestures dialog.

The braille display can now automatically scroll, and DotPad devices support multi-button combinations. The default gesture to toggle automatic scroll is NVDA+alt+k .

Liblouis has been updated with new Italian and Estonian braille tables. When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration.

Download the new version from the NVDA 2026.2 release post (or by checking for updates from within NVDA).

As well as the article below, and a new extensive section on the magnifier in the User Guide, our “Basic Training for NVDA” module has been updated with a number of updates. Of particular interest is a new section on the magnifier, there is also a topic covering reading the last spoken information and other new and improved content. These new updates are currently only available in the electronic text version. You can purchase Basic Training for NVDA from our shop . If you have already purchased the module, you can download the new version with the Magnifier section from the downloads page after logging into your NV Access account .

We are very excited to incorporate a magnifier into NVDA for the first time. We have had a lot of comments from users who are excited for this feature, and we’ve had some questions too, so let’s cover off some of the things it can and cannot do, and why it is a useful addition to NVDA:

First Release Firstly, it’s worth highlighting that this is the first release of NVDA with a magnifier and so the features will improve over time. We try to ship NVDA features incrementally, keeping the initial design scope small and allowing for early user feedback. This allows us to grow the magnifier in response to user reaction. Currently NVDA only works as a full-screen magnifier. We plan to extend the options in future releases. Adding windowed / docked modes is a high priority once bugs are addressed and the full-screen mode is more polished.

What CAN the magnifier do? The magnifier has most of the features you might expect from such a feature: You can zoom in and out (from 1x up to 50x) The view will follow the mouse, keyboard focus, browse mode focus and NVDA navigator object and review cursor – user selectable You can pan the view with the keyboard, in configurable increments, or jump to the edges of the screen You can adjust the colours (normal, inverted or greyscale) You can choose how objects are tracked (Centred or relative to their position on screen) You can configure the keystrokes for the various functions There is a keystroke to briefly zoom out and show an overview of the screen

We have made a short demo of the magnification feature on our YouTube channel .

Should I change magnifiers? Particularly if you currently use another magnification solution, we very much encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier. We are interested in your feedback, and particularly where you would like to see our feature improve.

If you already use Windows magnifier or another program, you can keep using it and it will continue to work with NVDA’s speech functions. Just as we don’t recommend having two screen readers running at once, we also wouldn’t recommend having NVDA’s magnifier AND another magnifier running at the same time.

If you do currently use Windows Magnifier, some of the reasons you may consider NVDA’s magnifier: It starts when NVDA starts (once you enable it) Configurable keystrokes Greyscale colour filtering mode Relative tracking mode Ability to follow NVDA’s object navigation and review cursor Keys to jump to edges of screen No settings window always on screen Ability to set your desired settings once and save to a portable copy you can use on any computer

If you use Windows magnifier in docked or lens mode, or some of the other features which haven’t yet made it into the NVDA magnifier in NVDA 2026.2, then you may wish to stay with Windows magnifier for now – but we do encourage you to try out the NVDA magnifier and let us know what you think.

Before we even got this edition of In-Process finished, to tell you all about 2026.2…. we ALREADY have a new beta? Of NVDA 2026.3 ? Yep! And I’m not going to talk about that yet – if you want to check it out, please head to the beta release announcement . What I did want to briefly mention, was how we came to have a new beta out, when the paint isn’t even dry on NVDA 2026.2?

Great question! And it comes down to how we develop software. Both our internal developers, and the community are constantly working on improving features, fixing bugs, and adding new things into NVDA. As a new piece of code gets incorporated into NVDA, it goes into an “Alpha” build – an early pre-release build with whatever has been changed recently. This lets our developers and our most dedicated testers try it out and give feedback. These come out almost daily (and sometimes several in one day). Because of the quick turnaround, we don’t share them on social media or here on the blog, but if you’d like to try them out, alpha builds are publicly available from the snapshots page . Be aware that they may not be as polished as the stable releases – though the process to test them out is identical.

So, generally a week after a stable release, we collate all the things which have been in alpha for at least a couple of weeks, and put them together into a “beta” release of the next version. While we may still have some features we are working on for later betas, as well any regressions or major issues discovered from the previous release, we can turn much of our development attention on towards the NEXT release.

So, if you ever find an issue with NVDA, the sooner you let us know, the sooner we can prioritise it and work on a fix as needed.

One of the perhaps less glamourous updates in NVDA 2026.2 is to a feature you hopefully don’t ever need to use.

“When resetting NVDA to factory defaults, an Undo button is now available to restore the previous configuration”

We’ve covered resetting NVDA to factory defaults previously , though it is worth being aware of. While something you hopefully don’t need, if you ever DO need it, it’s good to know it exists. With this new change, if you reset NVDA to factory defaults, a dialog appears advising “Your configuration has been reset to factory defaults. Choose OK to keep factory defaults, or Undo to restore your previous configuration”. This could be useful just in case you ever inadvertently activate the wrong item on the NVDA menu for instance, and may hopefully save you from needing go through setting up NVDA to your preferences again.

That’s all for this week, do update to NVDA 2026.2 if you haven’t already, and we’d love to hear your feedback on the new features – the magnifier of course, but also the other updates.

Muy atentos: Después de casi dos años de desarrollo, por fin llega TCA ConvertDoc 1.5. No es una simple actualización: es un salto generacional con las funcionalidades que me habéis ido pidiendo en los comentarios del blog, sobre todo desde la entrada de la versión 1.4. Para quienes aún no lo conozcan: ¿Qué es TCA ConvertDoc? TCA ConvertDoc es una pequeña utilidad portable y gratuita para Windows, con interfaz 100% accesible y atajos de teclado, que nos permite convertir entre multitud de formatos de documentos (doc, docx, RTF, epub, pdf, HTML, odt, txt, markdown, PNG, JPG, PPTx), hacer OCR a imágenes y PDFs, y ahora, además, traducir. Y todo, de forma individual o por lotes (carpeta entera de una sola vez). Pues bien, la 1.5 llega cargada de novedades. Os las cuento todas. Novedades de TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 1. Conversión DOCX → PDF (individual y por lotes) Ahora podéis convertir documentos de Word a PDF con un solo clic. ¿Tenéis una carpeta llena de? docx? La conversión masiva procesa todo el directorio de golpe, manteniendo el formato, las imágenes y la estructura del documento. Perfecto para preparar entregas, archivar o compartir. 2. Conversión PPTX → Markdown (individual y por lotes) Algunos me preguntasteis en la entrada de la 1.4 por qué ciertas presentaciones de PowerPoint no se pueden leer con lectores de pantalla. Pues esta es una de las soluciones: extrae el contenido de tus presentaciones a Markdown limpio y editable, ideal para documentación, blogs, wikis o migrar contenido. También funciona en lote para carpetas completas. 3. PDF escaneado PDF buscable (OCR) "¿Se puede convertir un pdf en un pdf con capacidad de búsqueda?" — me preguntasteis en los comentarios de la 1.4. ¡Ahora sí! Añades un PDF que es solo imagen (un escaneo sin capa de texto), TCA ConvertDoc le aplica OCR y te devuelve un PDF con texto seleccionable y buscable. Accesibilidad real para documentos heredados, del tipo que sea. 4. JPG / PNG PDF buscable Construye PDFs accesibles a partir de imágenes sueltas. Cada imagen pasa por OCR y se une en un único PDF donde puedes buscar, copiar y seleccionar el texto. Ideal para digitalizar notas, facturas, páginas de libros o documentos fotografiados con el móvil. 5. Traducción integrada! (¡la gran novedad!) Llevaba muchísimo tiempo queriendo incorporarle la traducción a TCA ConvertDoc, y por fin está aquí. Ahora el programa es capaz de traducir archivos completos a cualquier idioma usando dos motores: • Argos Translate | Offline | Descarga previa de los paquetes de idioma (privacidad total, sin internet) • Google Translate | Online | Conexión a internet, máxima calidad Formatos soportados: .txt, .docx y .pdf. Y lo mejor de todo: traduce incluso archivos grandes como libros enteros. El motor procesa el texto en fragmentos inteligentes, mantiene la estructura del documento (párrafos, saltos de página, estilos en DOCX) y te entrega el archivo traducido listo para usar. Nada de copiar y pegar por trozos, ni de chocar con límites ridículos de caracteres. Un detalle importante sobre Argos: la primera vez que uses Argos con un idioma, te aparecerá un diálogo ofreciéndote descargar los paquetes de ese idioma... y solo esa única vez. A partir de ahí, ese idioma queda instalado en el programa y funciona totalmente sin conexión. Tranquilo, no te lo volverá a pedir. 6. Selector de idiomas del OCR (Tesseract) completo En la 1.4 teníamos 3 idiomas de OCR (español, inglés e italiano). Ahora, en el cuadro combinado de idioma del OCR aparecen todos los idiomas que soporta Tesseract. Ya no hay que editar configs a mano ni adivinar códigos: eliges el idioma y listo. 7. Arreglos y optimizaciones internas OCR de archivos grandes: se ha reescrito el proceso para manejar PDFs e imágenes de gran tamaño sin agotar la memoria ni bloquear la interfaz. Gestión de hilos optimizada en las conversiones por lotes. Mejor detección de orientación y enderezado automático en imágenes escaneadas. Logs más claros y barra de progreso real en las operaciones largas. Y muchas otras mejoras internas que hacen el programa más estable y rápido. Requisitos para utilizar TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: • Windows10 (x64) en adelante. • portable, sin instalación. • Para Argos: el programa te ofrece descargar los paquetes del idioma la primera vez que lo uses (un solo diálogo), y luego funciona offline • Para Google Translate: conexión a internet Tip: si vas a trabajar mucho con traducción offline, entra a Argos, descarga de una vez los idiomas que más uses (español, inglés, francés, alemán, chino, japonés, árabe...) y olvídate. Luego todo irá 100% sin conexión. Tutorial: 📘 TCA ConvertDoc 1.5: OCR en PDF, 🚀 traduce libros y más! En este tutorial les mostraré: • Les mostraré la nueva conversión de Docx a PDF. • Conversión de PPTX a Markdown. • Conversión de un PDF (que son imágenes) a un PDF accesible (que admite búsqueda). • Construir un archivo PDF a partir de imágenes Jpg o PNG. • Muestra de que todos los idiomas ahora se cargan en el Motor OCR Tesseract. • Como traducir un documento en formato TXT a otro idioma de forma Online usando Google Translate (• conversión del inglés al español). • Como traducir un documento en formato Docx, utilizando la traducción OfLine con Argos Translate (• muestra del inglés al francés, descarga de idiomas y más). • Finalmente les mostraré, como traducir un PDF a otro idioma. La descarga. Les dejaré en la descarga: • El audio tutorial (en los canales Odysse y YouTube estará en video tutorial). • El programa TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 x64. • Archivo con las librerías visual estudio C++. Espero les sea de mucha utilidad: Dos años son mucho tiempo en software, pero TCA ConvertDoc 1.5 llega para quedarse. No es un parche: es un salto que cubre el ciclo completo —convertir, OCR, buscar, traducir— en una sola herramienta accesible, portable, gratuita y sin suscripciones. Si trabajas con documentos, investigas, digitalizas archivo o necesitas mover contenido entre idiomas, esta versión te va a ahorrar horas. es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la beta 1 de NVDA 2026.3 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Si quieres saber qué ofrece la próxima versión de NVDA antes de que se libere oficialmente, no dudes en descargar esta beta y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción. Al instalar esta beta te unirás al canal beta, y sólo recibirás avisos de actualización de compilaciones beta y candidatas a liberación (rc). El canal beta/rc siempre te mantendrá al día con la versión más reciente de NVDA. La última rc de un ciclo de liberación es idéntica a la última versión estable. Para regresar al canal de versiones estables, instala a mano la última versión estable.

Esta versión incorpora importantes mejoras de rendimiento, mejoras en los diálogos de NVDA, y entrada expandida por la pantalla táctil. Se han hecho varias mejoras para reducir los retrasos y aumentar el rendimiento. Ahora NVDA recupera y captura más información sobre los controles en segundo plano, mejorando el rendimiento en controles como cuadros combinados y el explorador de archivos. NVDA ya no hace que se rompan el explorador de archivos u otras aplicaciones al cerrarlo o reiniciarlo. NVDA se recupera ahora más rápido cuando una aplicación deja de responder, y ya no se colgará ni inundará el registro con errores en aplicaciones que no responden. En regiones vivas de texto, como las terminales, NVDA ya no se cuelga cuando se vuelcan en pantalla importantes cantidades de texto. Se han añadido menús de contexto y atajos de teclado a los diálogos de perfiles de configuración, gestos de entrada y diccionarios del habla, haciendo que estos diálogos sean más fáciles de usar con el teclado. Ahora también es posible cambiar directamente un gesto existente en el diálogo Gestos de entrada. Se ha modernizado el diálogo que presenta mensajes explorables y ahora soporta mejor cambiar su tamaño, maximizarlo y minimizarlo. Se ha expandido significativamente la entrada por pantalla táctil. Los gestos de dos deslizamientos secuenciales ahora combinan dos deslizamientos en rápida sucesión en un solo gesto, incrementando enormemente la cantidad de gestos asociables. También se soportan ahora los gestos de borde, permitiendo que los gestos que comiencen a 15 mm de cualquier borde de la pantalla se asocien independientemente de los mismos gestos realizados en el centro de la pantalla. Se ha añadido una nueva orden sin asignar para mover el cursor del ratón al centro de la vista ampliada. Se puede usar el OCR de Windows con la lupa o la cortina de pantalla activadas. Se ha actualizado Liblouis con nuevas tablas braille en Elfdaliano, sami, maorí, braille unificado inglés de Nueva Zelanda, y aitiano criollo, una tabla noruega para texto en español, y variantes adicionales de sueco de 6 y 8 puntos. Se ha actualizado Espeak NG añadiendo soporte para liguriano y abkhaz. Para instalar esta beta, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.3 beta 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 288e684536edb011710d760fc18ba7b652241085742e304e17d8ee01ede2d20f. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera beta de NVDA 2026.3 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .

en.body:
A recent Microsoft update is changing how accessibility support is enabled for applications that use certain Microsoft web technologies. As a result, JAWS may not receive the information it needs from these applications, causing some features to provide no speech or braille.

This may affect:

The issue is not currently observed in web browsers such as Chrome, Edge, and Firefox.

If you find that JAWS is not working as expected in web-based apps, toggle the Touch Cursor on and off again for JAWS to resume speaking normally. To enable the Touch Cursor, press SHIFT+NUM PAD PLUS if using Desktop keyboard layout and CAPS LOCK+SHIFT+SEMICOLON if using Laptop keyboard layout. To toggle it off and return to the Virtual PC Cursor, press NUM PAD PLUS twice quickly (in Desktop layout) or hold CAPS LOCK and press SEMICOLON twice quickly in Laptop layout.

If the content still does not respond as expected, press F5 to refresh the page or application content.

Vispero is working directly with Microsoft to investigate the issue and determine the appropriate fix. We will provide additional information when it becomes available.

es.body:
¡Hola, comunidad! ¿Cómo han ido estos meses de descanso? Esperamos que hayan servido para cargar las pilas y empezar este nuevo año lectivo con energía. Nosotros, aunque no hemos desconectado del todo para informarte de la llegada de NVDA 2026.2 y actualizar traducciones, estamos listos para seguir adelante con nuestra actividad habitual. Si recuerdas el anuncio de la beta 7 de NVDA 2026.2 , vino acompañado de una mala noticia: el fallecimiento de Rui Fontes, miembro muy activo de la comunidad a nivel internacional y propietario de Tiflotecnia, la compañía que actualmente comercializa las voces más recientes de Vocalizer para NVDA. Tras este triste anuncio, la venta de las voces quedó en pausa, a la espera de que se aclarase la situación en Tiflotecnia. Desde NVDA.es nos complace anunciar que dicha aclaración ya ha tenido lugar, y por tanto volvemos a reactivar la venta de este sintetizador de voz rápido y de alta calidad. En consecuencia, ya puedes volver a adquirir licencias completas por 90 euros, y actualizaciones de licencias de la versión 3 a la 4 por 50 euros, en ambos casos con impuestos incluidos. Recuerda que cada licencia te permitirá usar el sintetizador en hasta tres equipos de forma simultánea. Si vas a formatear o quieres hacer cambios relevantes de hardware, puedes devolver tu licencia al servidor para recuperarla más adelante. Además, es posible activar y desactivar licencias en equipos que no disponen de conexión a Internet, algo que con la versión 3.0 no se podía hacer. Y por si fuera poco, una sola licencia incluye todas las voces disponibles, ¡en todos los idiomas y con todas las calidades! Si todavía no lo has hecho, puedes instalar y probar estas voces sin coste alguno durante una semana. Te animamos a hacerlo, ¡la experiencia merece la pena! ¡Hasta la próxima!

Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la versión final de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tras 11 versiones beta y 2 candidatas a liberación, NV Access ha anunciado mediante esta publicación que ya se encuentra disponible para su descarga la versión final de NVDA 2026.2, el lector de pantalla gratuito y de código abierto para Microsoft Windows. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios actualizar a esta nueva versión, cuyo uso se considera apto también en entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de magnificador integrado, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y una ampliación de funciones de voz y braille. El magnificador ofrece opciones de aumentos y de filtrado de colores para ayudar a los usuarios con discapacidad visual. Actualmente, el Magnificador solo es compatible con el modo a pantalla completa, aunque en una futura actualización se prevé la incorporación de modos acoplados. Se ha ampliado considerablemente la compatibilidad táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizco y la navegación por el contenido web mediante el modo táctil. Ahora puedes desplazarte entre enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos mediante gestos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con la compatibilidad con diccionarios de voz personalizados que pueden proporcionarse mediante complementos, así como con nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que permiten un control más preciso. Se ha añadido una nueva configuración de voz para las voces de OneCore con el fin de controlar las pausas tras los signos de puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la posibilidad de mostrarla en un mensaje que se pueda leer. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información leída en voz alta es NVDA+x, que se puede modificar en el cuadro de diálogo «Gestos de entrada». Ahora, la pantalla braille puede desplazarse automáticamente y los dispositivos DotPad admiten combinaciones de varios botones. El atajo predeterminado para activar o desactivar el desplazamiento automático es NVDA+Alt+k. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas de braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer las opciones predeterminadas de fábrica de NVDA, ahora hay disponible un botón «Deshacer» para recuperar la configuración anterior. Consulta todas las novedades aquí Tan pronto como actualices NVDA, no olvides reiniciar el equipo. El reinicio garantiza que se pueden actualizar archivos que antes no se podían modificar porque estaban abiertos para escritura. En la práctica, al reiniciar vuelven a funcionar aplicaciones basadas en Electron, tales como Teams, Dropbox o Google Drive, y dejan de producirse comportamientos extraños con el explorador de archivos, Thunderbird, Office y algunos navegadores. Reiniciar es lo primero que debes hacer antes de informar de cualquier fallo. Hazlo pulsando windows+d para ir al escritorio, alt+f4, e intro sobre la opción Reiniciar. Puedes descargar NVDA 2026.2, así como las últimas versiones compatibles con sistemas antiguos y material útil para desarrolladores, desde nuestra página de descargas . La suma SHA256 de NVDA 2026.2, que se usa para garantizar la integridad de la descarga, es f3f8d29974a88d687b3c4809be192219ec579c5bdabcda5aaf53635288bca824. Si tienes una versión estable anterior, también puedes actualizar automáticamente desde el menú Ayuda. Y desde la rc2, con el complemento Selector del canal de actualización, se puede hacer del mismo modo configurando previamente el canal estable. Si todavía no conoces NVDA y quieres leer algo más sobre él antes de probarlo, te recomendamos consultar la guía de usuario y la referencia rápida de órdenes . Si te gustan nuestros proyectos y el contenido que ofrecemos, plantéate contribuir mensualmente con una pequeña cantidad. Tan sólo un euro es capaz de marcar la diferencia y ayudarnos a mejorar. Visita la página de donaciones para obtener más información, o la tienda para hacerte con libros de formación traducidos y sintetizadores de voz de alta calidad. ¡Feliz lunes!

Web Accessibility In Mind (WebAIM) is surveying screen reader users to collect information that will impact the future development of web content and web standards. WebAIM, part of Utah State University, provides training, tools, and information to assist in the creation of websites that are accessible to individuals with disabilities.

Web accessibility is crucial to ensure screen reader users can readily access information on the web. This includes content such as:

Websites are often used to shop online, complete school assignments, and perform essential work tasks. This makes accessibility a necessary part of website development.

Whether you consider yourself a novice or an advanced JAWS user, we ask that you contribute to the future of web accessibility by taking the WebAIM Screen Reader Survey . It will remain open through Monday, August 31, 2026 , and takes around five to ten minutes to complete.

en.title: In-Process 24th August 2026
en.summary: We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around: NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! Automatically Scrolling the Braille Display Getting help from others New Unassigned Commands Finding out more about what is new NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate! The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all… Read More
en.body:
We’re so close to 2026.2 now! We have a release candidate! Plus, this time around:

The NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate is now available for testing! We encourage all users to download this RC and provide feedback. Unless any critical bugs are found, this will be identical to the final 2026.2 release.

NVDA 2026.2 includes:

Magnifier (full screen, colour filtering, zoom, focus tracking) Improved touch gestures (links, form fields, etc) NVDA+x to repeat last spoken information Improved speech dictionaries Automatic Braille Display scrolling & much more!

We would encourage you to try out the NVDA 2026.2 Release Candidate , especially if you haven’t yet tried any of the betas. You can do this by creating a portable copy or by selecting “Continue running” from the launcher, to run a temporary copy and not interfere with your installed copy of NVDA.

One of the new features in NVDA 2026.2, is that we: “Added the ability to automatically scroll the braille display”. This comes courtesy of Noelia, one of our prominent Spanish contributors. Reading the user guide entry for the new “Automatic scroll rate” feature, it notes:

Automatic braille scrolling can be enabled to scroll the display at a set speed. When using this feature, the braille display scrolls to present information which is more than will fit on the display at once. The feature is disabled by default. You can change the gestures assigned to use automatic braille scrolling in NVDA’s Input Gestures dialog before it can be used. Gestures are also available to speed up or slow down the rate of automatic scrolling. Alternatively, you can set the automatic scroll rate in Braille Settings.

While braille is scrolling, you can still use the scroll back and scroll forward commands without stopping scrolling. Scroll back can be useful to read previous contents again. Scroll forward can be useful to skip a blank line, or if the line being read is short.

While reading, automatic braille scrolling will stop when any of the following happen:

The toggle automatic braille scrolling key is pressed The user presses a key or gesture which would display a new message The focus is moved (including with braille display panning keys) The end of the document is reached The state of the lock or secure screen is changed (such as the computer being locked)

The commands for this feature are: Toggle automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+k Increase automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+L Decrease automatic scroll: NVDA+alt+j

Last fortnight, we covered ways you can get help from within NVDA itself. This time around, let’s have a look at some of the places you can get help from others. As with last fortnight’s post, this list covers getting help for NVDA itself only, aimed at end users: NV Access Telephone Support : If you’ve still got questions after following last fortnight’s tips and reading Basic Training for NVDA etc, give us a call. Telephone support IS a paid service, and for end-user support only, but it is available 24/7. We have numbers you can call in Australia or the USA, OR you can email us and we can call you anywhere in the world. You also get telephone support included with the NVDA Productivity Bundle . Official NVDA Email Group : While we monitor various other groups, the one place you know you will find NV Access staff, and users, is the official, friendly, NVDA email group at https://nvaccess.org/nvda-users – plus, as a free, welcoming and popular resource, you will often get help from other users even quicker than we can respond. Local language email groups : We have a huge list of email groups in many languages. Know of a group which isn’t listed? Please, let us know so we can share it on the connect page for others! Social media : Our community on Mastodon is the most active, but you can also find us on Facebook and other platforms . NVDA Remote Access : Have a friend who can help with your PC? You can let them connect to your PC to help you. Note there are a number of security measures in place to ensure this feature can only be accessed by deliberate action from both parties.

For the upcoming NVDA 2026.2, we’ve added a couple of new “unassigned” commands. These aren’t always the most obvious to find, so I thought it was worth highlighting them here: Added an unassigned command to toggle keyboard layout. ( #19211 , @CyrilleB79 ) Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z ) Added an unassigned command to report the current status of the Screen Curtain. ( #19759 )

Commands like these can provide useful functionality, but may often only be required by some users. As we are all aware, screen readers already have a lot of keystrokes, so we always have to think carefully before assigning new keystrokes.

For instance, the toggle keyboard layout setting. Most users will setup the keyboard layout how they prefer, and never need to change it. For the rare time you may wish to change it, the setting is on the keyboard settings page, which is available with NVDA+control+k . For testing or teaching, a command to toggle the layout on the fly may be invaluable, so, in NVDA 2026.2, it’s there if you need it.

In any NVDA release announcement , there is a link to “ What’s new in this release of NVDA ” (I’ve linked to those to things for NVDA 2026.2 RC1). That document gives a summary of the highlights in several paragraphs, and then bullet points for all the changes in groups: Important notes : information such as older Windows versions no longer supported Security fixes : Updates to NVDA which fix potential security issues. New features : New functionality in NVDA. For instance, NVDA+x to repeat the last spoken information, or the ability to automatically scroll the braille display Changes : Features which may be slightly different, such as renaming the “COM Registration Fixing Tool” to “System Accessibility Repair Tool”. Bug fixes : Fixing features which didn’t work the way they should. For instance, in NVDA 2026.2, we’ve fixed a crash in the add-on store, NVDA now recovers quicker from freezes in some applications, and form controls are correctly reported in Firefox again. Changes for developers : Updates which may affect how contributors code for NVDA. These don’t affect end users directly. For instance, updating the version of Python used, or new functions developers can call to find out information. Deprecations : Again, only for developers, function calls which either no longer work, or have been changed to something else, and developers should transition over to the new function call.

In most of the bullet points for each release, there is a number at the end, and sometimes a username. For instance, in the unassigned commands article above: “Added an unassigned Quick Navigation Command for jumping to next/previous slider in browse mode. ( #17005 , @tareh7z )”

In this case, #17005 is the issue number assigned to the original request for this feature. @tareh7z is the GitHub user who wrote the code and submitted the pull request to fix it – thanks @tareh7z! And thanks to ALL our contributors. NVDA 2026.2 is a big release with a lot of amazing features the community have put a lot of work into!

The line in the changes document will hopefully give enough information to quickly describe the feature for most users. The user guide will also have been updated with any relevant information. In this case, look at section 6.1.3 “Other Navigation Commands”, which talks about not only sliders, but other quick navigation commands which don’t have default keystrokes.

The issue number is a link back to that issue, which can be helpful if you’d like to look back at the conversation which prompted the new feature. For instance, in this case, there was some discussion around what other types of information could potentially be accessed with a “slider” command (others that were suggested were ruled out in this case).

That’s all for this time. Do please try out the NVDA 2026.2 release candidate , and of course, let us know of any issues you encounter with it. Next time around we will have more on NVDA 2026.2!

A menos … Continuar leyendo "Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2" La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
es.body:
Tal y como ha anunciado NV Access mediante esta publicación , la rc 1 de NVDA 2026.2 ya se encuentra disponible para descarga y pruebas. Se recomienda a todos los usuarios descargar esta versión y proporcionar comentarios por los canales de la comunidad, o por el sistema de informe de fallos de NV Access . A menos que se detecten fallos críticos de última hora, esta versión será idéntica a la versión final de NVDA 2026.2. Esta versión no es apta para entornos de producción.

Esta versión incluye una nueva función de ampliación, mejoras en los gestos táctiles y la navegación, y capacidades mejoradas de voz y braille. El ampliador proporciona opciones de zoom y filtro de color para asistir a usuarios con baja visión. Actualmente, el ampliador sólo soporta el modo a pantalla completa, dejando los modos acoplados planificados para una futura versión. Se ha expandido significativamente el soporte táctil con nuevos gestos de pellizcar y con navegación en modo exploración táctil en contenido web. Ahora se puede navegar por enlaces, encabezados, campos de formulario y otros elementos usando deslizamientos táctiles. Se han mejorado las funciones de voz con soporte de diccionarios del habla personalizados que pueden proporcionarse en complementos y nuevos tipos de entradas de diccionario que proporcionan un control más granular. Se ha añadido una nueva opción en las voces OneCore para controlar las pausas después de la puntuación. Una nueva orden permite repetir la última información verbalizada, con la capacidad de mostrarla en un mensaje explorable. El gesto predeterminado para repetir la última información verbalizada es NVDA+x, y se puede cambiar desde el diálogo Gestos de entrada. La pantalla braille ahora puede desplazarse automáticamente, y los dispositivos DotPad soportan combinaciones multibotón. Liblouis se ha actualizado con nuevas tablas braille en italiano y estonio. Al restablecer NVDA a los valores de fábrica, ahora hay disponible un botón de deshacer para restaurar la configuración anterior. Para instalar esta candidata a liberación, puedes configurar el canal «rc y beta» en el complemento Selector del canal de actualización y buscar actualizaciones desde el menú Ayuda de NVDA, o actualizar desde una beta anterior. Y como siempre, también puedes descargar manualmente el instalador de NVDA 2026.2 rc 1 . Su suma de comprobación SHA256, que te permitirá garantizar la integridad del archivo descargado, es 09dfba7e03f37598a50e8495370a063864acd4de48ce6ebdf9ee320c536803f5. ¡Feliz lunes!

La entrada Ya disponible la primera candidata a liberación de NVDA 2026.2 se publicó primero en NVDA en español .
